ProgramName: Master of Accounting
Requirements: Application requirements consist of the following: Graduate School Application, Application Fee ($85 for U.S. citizens and Permanent Residents or $95 for non-resident aliens and international applicants), Personal Statement, Three Letters of Recommendation, Resume, Transcripts (1 copy from all universities attended), and a minimum 530 GMAT score required. [2] The Admission Committee evaluates candidates on their undergraduate academic record, GMAT score, and engagement & leadership (including internship/work experience, student athletics, campus organizations, volunteer work, study abroad, leadership experience, and integrity). [1] A personal interview is also required as part of the application process, though it may be waived in certain circumstances. [2]
Description: The Jenkins Master of Accounting (MAC) program provides exceptional education and real-world experience that equip students to take their careers to the next level. Whether pursued on campus and in-person or taken entirely online, the program's curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of accounting and business practices, as well as a rigorous technical accounting education. Students have the choice of two tracks (public accounting or business and industry) to meets the needs of their career goals in the accounting profession. They can choose to complement these core courses with specializations an Enterprise Risk Management, Information Technology, or Tax Strategy. The curriculum is focused on both preparing you for the CPA exam and developing real-world skills, and learning doesn't stop in the classroom. MAC students can study abroad, lead financial literacy courses on campus or in the community, work with real companies in practicum exercises and take advantage of innovative learning opportunities.
Accredidation: The Poole College of Management is accredited by the AACSB. The Department of Accounting has also received supplemental accounting accreditation from the AACSB. [8, 15]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Adult and Community College Education
Requirements: To qualify for admission, applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in any field. [3] International applicants must also have a TOEFL score of 100 or higher. [3] Admission decisions are based on several criteria, including undergraduate GPA, work history and interest in the field. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Education in Adult and Community College Education
Requirements: Completed online application, department application form, resume and non-refundable application fee; Unofficial transcripts are to be uploaded into the application portal. [3] If admitted, official transcripts must be sent to the Graduate School before admission is confirmed. [3] Statement of interest including summary of your proposed program goals and desired future outcomes upon program completion; North Carolina residency form if claiming for tuition purposes; TOEFL or IELTS scores for international students; Three Letters of Recommendation. [3]
Concentration: ['Adult and Continuing Professional Education', 'Community College Teaching', 'Health Professions Education']
Description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Adult and Community College Education is designed for entering and experienced educators who seek to advance their careers. Our degree program integrates the best of established adult and lifelong education topics with emerging professional fields. [3] Our program prepares graduates in key subject areas such as understanding adult learner characteristics, motivations, barriers and opportunities; the study of how adults learn, change and grow and how they can be supported by others to do so; the role of technology and distance education in adult learning; and, how professionals can build capacities to design, assess, lead and change organizations that serve adult learners. [3, 4] Adults learn in many contexts – postsecondary and college settings, training & professional development, workplace and workforce development, and in helping profession contexts such as community education, adult basic education, non-profit, religious, or health professions. [3, 6] Note: Degrees earned will be distributed as: "Master of Education in Adult and Community College Education" without focus area track specifications. [3, 8]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Adult and Community College Education
Requirements: To qualify for admission, applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in any field. Admission decisions are based on several criteria, including undergraduate GPA, work history, and interest in the field. A completed online application, department application form, resume, statement of interest, three letters of recommendation, and a non-refundable application fee are required. Unofficial transcripts are to be uploaded into the application portal. International applicants must have a TOEFL score of 100 or higher. [2, 10]
Concentration: ['Adult and Continuing Professional Education Track', 'Community College Teaching Track', 'Health Professions Education Track']
Description: The Master of Science in Adult and Community College Education is designed for those who want to teach students in community colleges and those who want to work with adult learners. [6] The program is available on the NCSU campus and online. [6]
Accredidation: The College of Education is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Counseling and Related Programs (CACREP) and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). [3] All of the bachelor's level and graduate level licensure programs are approved by the North Carolina State Board of Education. [3] North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctorate degrees. [8]

ProgramName: Master of Advanced Architectural Studies
Requirements: The application requires a portfolio of work, uploaded unofficial transcripts for each institution attended, three uploaded letters of recommendation, a resume, and a Research Interest Statement of 750 words or less. [3]
Fees.1: No change to the approved tuition, tuition differential, or fees from the existing Master of Architecture program is requested. [32]
Description: The Master of Advanced Architectural Studies is a three-semester, research-based innovative program for committed, self-directed a professional degree in architecture, or a degree in a related discipline. It provides opportunities for specialized study in leading-edge areas of the built environment, and a platform to explore solutions to the crucial issues of the 21st century. Students in the MAAS program work closely with a faculty advisor with expertise in students' areas of study during the duration of their program.
Accredidation: This degree is not accredited by the National Architecture Accrediting Board (NAAB). [7]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant must have a four-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited institution with at least a 'B' (3.000/4.000) average in their undergraduate major or latest graduate degree. [7] For the PhD program specifically, a GPA of at least 3.3 on a 4.0 scale in a master's program is required, or 3.5 for Direct to PhD applicants without a prior MS. [8] Applicants need to provide three satisfactory letters of recommendation. [8] For international applicants, TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo scores are necessary unless a waiver is granted. [8]
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree is pursued by outstanding students with an intense interest in independent study and research. It consists of advanced coursework beyond the master's degree, a written and oral comprehensive preliminary examination, extended and in-depth research, a written dissertation, and a final oral defense of the research.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Student Support Plan (GSSP) which includes tuition support and health insurance for students with teaching or research assistantships.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Overall grade point average (GPA) of >3.0 on a 4.0 scale from an accredited institution; Undergraduate major in a technical area which satisfies the prerequisites for graduate coursework in MAE; Three satisfactory letters of recommendation.
Description: The Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering (MSAE) distance education program is designed for professionals with degrees in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering or a closely related fields who wish to study aerospace structures, materials and control, aerodynamics, fluid mechanics, and propulsion. [6]

ProgramName: Certificate in Agricultural and Extension Education
Requirements: Applicants must meet one of these requirements for admission to the graduate certificate program: Be a graduate of an accredited four-year college or university with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 at the time of graduation, or. Be a degree student in good standing in a NC State University graduate program. [1, 2]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The Department of Agricultural and Extension Education offers a Graduate Certificate in Agricultural and Extension Education. [1] The program focuses on developing knowledge and skills needed to be effective teachers of agriculture in the public schools and community colleges or to work as an educator with the Cooperative Extension Service or in other non-formal educational settings such as public gardens, nature centers and in international development. [1, 3] The AEE certificate program is appropriate for individuals who: have a master's degree in another discipline but would like to gain expertise in agricultural and extension education; are earning a teacher certification in agriculture and desire additional credentials; or work as an extension agent or in another community setting, and need to take courses for required professional development credits. [1] The certificate program involves the completion of 15 credit hours. [1, 3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Agricultural and Extension Education
Requirements: Minimum 3.5 a graduate GPA for doctoral students; Three letters of recommendation (At least one academic reference); For doctoral applicants: 1-year required experience, 3 years recommended. Relevant experience in extension, teaching, industry, leadership, or other closely related fields. [3]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: In the Ph.D. in Agricultural Education and Human Sciences program, students can specialize in several areas of focus, including: Agricultural Education, Extension Education, Agricultural Leadership Development, and Family and Community Sciences. [2]
Description: The Department of Agricultural and Human Sciences at NC State offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Agricultural Education and Human Sciences (AEHS). [2] It is a rigorous, research-based program designed for students who want to pursue careers in higher education or administrative positions in educational settings or government. [2] The program is designed to be customized to meet each student's career goals. [2] The curriculum encompasses all aspects of the Department of Agricultural and Human Sciences (AHS): leadership, agricultural extension, agricultural education, and family and community sciences. [6] A minimum of 72 hours past the Bachelor's degree is required, which includes at least six hours of statistics, six hours of additional research breadth coursework, and twelve hours for the dissertation. [8] Doctoral students are expected to achieve mastery of knowledge in their field, produce superior quality work, and demonstrate the ability to conduct original research. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Agricultural and Extension Education
Requirements: Minimum 3.0 undergraduate GPA for master's students; Three letters of recommendation (At least one academic reference); Personal statement; Relevant experience in extension, teaching, industry, leadership, or other closely related fields; Transcripts of all previous collegiate work; Application fee. [1]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: Prepare for a career teaching agricultural education to middle or high school students, or become an Extension agent helping farmers and families succeed in their communities. Or pursue other rewarding positions such as agricultural museum curators, environmental educators, agricultural missionaries, agricultural public relations representatives, or congressional officers.In the M.S. program, students gain practical experience in conducting research. [10] Upon completion, students with a teaching emphasis may qualify for a master's level (M) teaching license. [10]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award the associate, baccalaureate, masters and doctorate degrees. [6]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Agricultural and Extension Education
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: ['Agricultural Education', 'Extension Education', 'Agricultural Leadership Development', 'Family and Community Sciences']
Description: The Master of Science program within the Department of Agricultural and Human Sciences prepares students for diverse career options, including teaching agricultural education in middle or high schools, becoming Extension agents, or pursuing other roles such as agricultural museum curators, environmental educators, and agricultural public relations representatives. The program is designed to create leaders who support agriculture, youth, and families, with graduates working in formal and non-formal settings, non-profits, community and government agencies, and various fields of agriculture and human sciences. The M.S. degree is a thesis-based track requiring 36 credit hours, and students work with an advisory committee to select appropriate elective courses.
Accredidation: The program is offered by North Carolina State University, which is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC).
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $2,500

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Science
Requirements: We consider applicants for admission to our graduate programs on a number of factors, including undergraduate coursework, GRE scores, relevant experience, and letters of reference. Final admission requires an applicant to obtain the commitment from a graduate faculty advisor to take the applicant into their training program. A complete graduate application package includes: Graduate School application; Official transcripts from all undergraduate institutions attended; GRE scores; TOEFL scores (international students only) The overall TOEFL score must be a minimum of 80 with a score of 18 in each category with no appeals. A statement of interest; Three (3) letters of reference; Application fee.
Description: A doctoral degree in Animal Science and Poultry Science with a concentration in either Animal Science or Poultry Science is offered. [8] Specific course requirements are flexible and each student's program is developed in consultation with their Ph.D. advisory committee. [8] The minor is optional but if a minor is included, external faculty representation is required on the advisory committee. [8]

ProgramName: Master of Animal Science
Requirements: A complete graduate application package includes: a Graduate School application, official transcripts from all undergraduate institutions attended, GRE scores, TOEFL scores for international students, a statement of interest, and three letters of reference. The overall TOEFL score must be a minimum of 80 with a score of 18 in each category. Final admission requires an applicant to obtain the commitment from a graduate faculty advisor. Applicants should have an undergraduate degree in Animal Science or a related field, with a competitive GPA (3.0 or higher). Prerequisites include a background or coursework in physiology, chemistry, biochemistry, and genetics.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Fees.1: The university catalog does not specify a unique tuition fee for the Master of Animal Science program, so it is presumed to follow the standard graduate tuition rates. Certain programs may carry a tuition premium, though Animal Science is not explicitly listed as one of them. [7, 10, 23]
Description: The Master of Animal Science nonthesis degree program is designed to give students a deeper academic background in sub-disciplines associated with the field of Animal Science which include nutrition, physiology, genetics, biotechnology and animal management. [4] The non-thesis Master of Animal Science (MR) degree (Option B) requires a minimum of 36 credit hours, 19 credits of core courses and 17 credits of elective courses. [2] The MR degree program is also offered through distance education. [2]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award the associate, baccalaureate, masters and doctorate degrees. [4, 6]
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the estimated graduate tuition is $568.33 per credit hour for North Carolina residents and $1,751.56 per credit hour for non-residents. [23]
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, traineeships, teaching assistantships, research assistantships, service assistantships, work-study programs, and loans. [9, 27]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Animal Science
Requirements: A complete graduate application package includes: Graduate School application, Official transcripts from all undergraduate institutions attended, GRE scores, TOEFL scores (international students only), a statement of interest, and three (3) letters of reference.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: North Carolina State University offers a Master of Science in Animal Science. The Animal Science Graduate Program is dedicated to training graduate students in multiple animal science disciplines. The program's underlying principles for students are to develop an appreciation for knowledge in animal physiology (such as ruminant and monogastric nutrition, reproduction, or stress), animal health, or animal well-being (including immunology, genomics, microbiology, pre-harvest food safety, or behavior). It also aims to help students achieve a foundation to use the scientific method for investigating fundamental problems in animal production and to enhance and refine their verbal and written communication skills. The program aims to provide comprehensive and individualized training to prepare students for the diverse field of animal science, which may require a mix of general and specific training tailored to individual career goals. The MS programs are flexible and of high quality, relying on a selection of courses in both allied sciences and the animal science area, combined with the planning, conducting, interpretation, and reporting of an original research project.

CostPerCredit: $1,599.10 per course

ProgramName: Certificate in Applied Ecology
Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Ecology
Requirements: All applications are submitted to the NC State Graduate School through the online application system. It is important that you identify a potential faculty advisor, as this will greatly increase your chance of admission. A graduate student will not be admitted to the Department of Applied Ecology for graduate studies unless he or she has identified a faculty advisor. Successful applicants usually have a bachelor's degree in a biological science with at least an overall 'B' average and a minimum number of courses in biology and supporting fields (6 in biology, 4 in chemistry, 2 in physics, and 2 in mathematics). For Ph.D. applicants, a GPA of at least 3.2 is expected. In addition to grades and coursework, the admissions committee considers relevant experience, statement of interest, and letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required. [2]
Description: The Ph.D. program in Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology allows doctoral students to pursue an advanced degree in a wide variety of subjects involving fisheries and wildlife, including topics that overlap with environmental resources, forestry and other specialty areas supported by the College of Natural Resources, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, and College of Veterinary Medicine. [1] Faculty and students in Fisheries, Wildlife and Conservation Biology conduct applied research to help guide sustainable solutions for conservation challenges locally, regionally and globally. [1] The program emphasizes habitat assessment, population biology, human dimensions, environmental policy, animal health, and sustainable management of fish and wildlife species. [2] The Ph.D. program requires 36 to 54 credits of course work beyond the master's degree, including two hours of seminar, FW 730 (Ethics in Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology), and a dissertation. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Applied Ecology
Requirements: Application for admission is made directly to the Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology program. Minimum requirements include an undergraduate grade point average of 3.0 in an appropriate biological discipline. Completion of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is optional, depending on the requirements of individual faculty. Admission is competitive and is contingent on the willingness of a member of the faculty to serve as the major professor. Exceptions to minimum requirements may be made for students with special backgrounds. [7]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Fees: The annual graduate tuition rate is $10,230 for North Carolina residents and $31,528 for nonresidents. Program-specific fees for the Master of Applied Ecology are not specified on the website.
Concentration: ['Master of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology (non-thesis)', 'Master of Science in Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology (thesis-based)']
Description: The Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology program at NC State University is a leader in fish and wildlife science and takes an interdisciplinary approach to education and research. [8] We employ cutting-edge research and work with a variety of partners to ensure common fish and wildlife species remain common, and threatened and endangered fish and wildlife species are saved. [8] The program focuses on researching and understanding ecological principles as they apply to natural resource management as well as the subsequent effects on wildlife, fisheries and aquaculture. [2, 8] The mission is to advance the scientifically-based conservation, management and use of fishery, wildlife and associated resources. [2, 8] The degrees emphasize habitat assessment, population biology, human dimensions, environmental policy, animal health, and sustainable management of fish and wildlife species. [6] This intercollegiate program is co-administered by the College of Natural Resources, the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, and the College of Veterinary Medicine. [3, 6]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Commission on Colleges of the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools to award associate, baccalaureate, master's and doctoral degrees. [9]
CostPerCredit: For residents, the cost per credit hour is $568.33 in tuition. For non-residents, the cost is $1,751.56 per credit hour. [26] This does not include additional fees.
ScholarshipAmount: The Supplemental Scholarships are for $2000.00 each. [11] The Harkema Scholarships average about $500, ranging from $250-$2,500. [15] The NCAUG Graduate Scholarship is for $1,500. [38] The NCWF Conservation Leadership Scholarship is for $2,500, with other awards of $1,000. [43]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships available to Applied Ecology students include those for enriching the graduate experience, such as for off-campus activities, and for students in specific research areas like GIS. [11, 15, 38]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Mathematics
Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture-based Enterprise Systems Engineering
Certificate in Assessment and Measurement
Doctor of Philosophy in Atmospheric Science
Requirements: A Bachelor's degree with research experience or a Master's degree is required for entry into the Ph.D. program. [37, 42] Applicants must hold an undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline such as natural science, engineering, or mathematics and have a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4-point scale. [36] The program requires a minimum of 72 credit hours beyond the B.S. or 54 credit hours beyond the M.S. (including research credits). [44]
Description: Graduate programs are offered in Atmospheric Science, Earth Science, and Marine Science. Specific course requirements are determined by the advisory committee of each student. Degrees earned will be distributed as: "Doctor of Philosophy in Marine, Earth, and Atmospheric Sciences" without track specifications.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Atmospheric Science
Requirements:
To be admitted to graduate study in Marine, Earth, and Atmospheric Sciences (MEAS), you must meet the following minimum requirements:
1. Hold an undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline of natural science, engineering, or mathematics.
2. Have a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent). In special circumstances applicants are sometimes admitted with a slightly lower GPA if other qualifications demonstrate excellence. [1]
Fees: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the tuition for residents of North Carolina is $5,115.00 for 9+ credit hours per semester, and for non-residents, it is $14,797.00 for 9+ credit hours per semester. [25] Additional fees apply. [25]
Description: Graduate programs are offered in Atmospheric Science, Earth Science, and Marine Science. Within marine sciences the subdisciplines include: biological, chemical, geological and physical oceanography. The M.S. degree requires a minimum of 30 credit hours. Specific course requirements are determined by the advisory committee of each student. However, MEA 601 Seminar is required of all thesis M.S. students no later than the third semester in residence. Marine science students are required to take core courses in two of the three subdisciplines other than their own. An M.S. degree with a non-thesis option for students is available and admission to this option must be requested at the time of application. [7]
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the tuition per credit hour for residents of North Carolina is $568.33 and for non-residents is $1,751.56. [25]
ScholarshipType: Most graduate students receive financial support through research and teaching assistantships. [13]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biochemistry
Requirements: Students entering the biochemistry graduate program have a bachelor's degree in biochemistry, chemistry or a related physical or biological science, including undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, calculus, physics and physical chemistry, as well as biochemistry or molecular biology. [1]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The objective of the Biochemistry Ph.D. program at North Carolina State University is to prepare students for careers as researchers primarily in academic, industrial, or government research environments. [10] Through a combination of coursework, seminars, and original research, students acquire the skills needed to become independent research scientists. [10] Students entering the program generally have a B.S. in biochemistry, chemistry, biology, genetics, or a related physical or biological science. [13] During the first year, students are advised by a graduate advisory committee and participate in coursework, teaching, and laboratory rotations. [13] Following core coursework, students can enroll in advanced courses chosen with their thesis advisor to support their thesis project. [13] Students also gain teaching experience as teaching assistants for one or more semesters and attend weekly departmental seminars. [13]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctorate degrees. [12, 14] The official university website does not mention a specific programmatic accreditation for the Doctor of Philosophy in Biochemistry program.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biochemistry
Requirements: Students entering the graduate program in biochemistry should have a bachelor's degree in biochemistry, chemistry or a related physical or biological science, including undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, calculus, physics and physical chemistry, as well as biochemistry/molecular biology. [30] We evaluate an applicant's complete file so there are no absolute minimum GPA or GRE scores. [22] Typically, admitted students have a GPA > 3.2 in biochemistry or a related field. [22] Applicants with a strong record of undergraduate research activity or with practical experience in a professional scientific setting are particularly encouraged to apply. [30]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Fees: $6,367.25/Semester
Fees.1: $5,115.00/Semester
Description: The Master's of Science is a research degree that prepares students in Biochemistry for Ph.D. studies or provides training for technical employment. [13] Through a combination of coursework, seminars, and original research, you will complete a Graduate degree and acquire the skills needed to become an independent research scientist. [13] The Master of Science is a research degree and students are required to defend their thesis research in a final oral examination. [5] Successful completion of the M.S. degree requires a minimum of 30 credit hours. [8]
CostPerCredit: $568.33/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Master of Bioinformatics
Requirements: Students applying to either the Master's or PhD program in Bioinformatics are evaluated on their background in three key areas: mathematics and statistics; genetics and biological sciences; and computer science. Students should have completed at least two semesters of calculus, and additional courses in mathematics and statistics are preferred. Evidence of basic computer programming skills is required. A course in genetics is strongly encouraged. Previous research experience is a significant advantage. [1]
Description: All studenten die een diploma in Bio-informatica en Functionele Genomica willen behalen, zullen een gedeeld kerncurriculum van cursussen volgen dat de breedte van kennis bevordert en interdisciplinaire samenwerking aanmoedigt. Studenten Functionele Genomica richten zich op laboratoriumonderzoek dat het verzamelen en interpreteren van massale datasets vereist die onze kennis van de biologie van organismen, genexpressie, eiwit- en nucleïnezuurstructuur en -functie, en genetische en omgevingsinteracties vergroten. Studenten Bio-informatica ontwikkelen vaardigheden om deze grote en complexe 'omics'-datasets te beher રાજ en te analyseren. Deze twee groepen studenten zullen worden voorbereid om naadloos samen te werken als onderdeel van teams die fundamenteel belangrijke problemen aanpakken op gebieden zoals de biowetenschappen, het fokken van planten en dieren, evolutionaire biologie, ecologie en toxicologie.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Bioinformatics
Requirements: Students applying to the PhD program in Bioinformatics are evaluated on their background in three key areas: mathematics and statistics; genetics and biological sciences; and computer science. Students should have completed at least two semesters of calculus, and additional courses in mathematics and statistics are preferred. Evidence of basic computer programming skills is required. A course in genetics is strongly encouraged. Previous research experience is a significant advantage. Required application materials include the application, a personal statement, all transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. International students may need to provide TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Description: All PhD students assemble advisory committees including faculty from both Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics to promote effective interdisciplinary research and collaboration, and many students have co-advisors representing different fields. [4] NC State offers two closely linked interdepartmental graduate programs in Genomic Sciences. [4] All students pursuing degrees in either Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics will take a shared core set of courses that promote breadth of knowledge and encourage interdisciplinary collaboration. [4] Functional Genomics students focus on laboratory research requiring the collection and interpretation of massive data sets that enhance our knowledge of organismal biology, gene expression, protein and nucleic acid structure and function, and genetic and environmental interactions. [4] Bioinformatics students develop skills to manage and analyze these large and complex “omics” data sets. [4] These two groups of students will be prepared to work seamlessly as parts of teams addressing fundamentally important problems in areas including the biomedical sciences, plant and animal breeding, evolutionary biology, ecology, and toxicology. [4] Unique and exceptional resources include the Bioinformatics Research Center and the Genome Research Laboratory. [4]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award the associate, baccalaureate, masters and doctorate degrees. [15]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biological and Agricultural Engineering
Requirements: A baccalaureate in biological or agricultural engineering or other engineering discipline (GPA > 2.8) is the preferred prerequisite for admission. [1] Those with a strong academic background in the physical or biological sciences may also be admitted with a requirement for undergraduate work in math, physics, chemistry and basic engineering courses. [1] In the case of applicants with Master's degrees, a Master's GPA of at least 3.2 is required for admission to the PhD. [1] Exceptions to the overall undergraduate GPA requirements may be made for cases where performance in the major or during the last two years was at or above the 3.00 level. [1] Applicants who do not have an engineering background, but have earned a degree in an appropriate science discipline may be admitted to the Systems Analysis Concentration in the MS or PhD program without completing the engineering prerequisites. [1] GRE scores are not required for admission. [1]
Description: The Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering's Master of Science degree is designed to develop new understanding through research and creativity. [1] Students have the option to pursue a thesis or non-thesis Master of Science degree. [1] Areas of specialization within the program include subject matter related to environmental and natural resources, food engineering, bioprocess engineering, biomaterials science, machine and energy systems, systems analysis along with food, feed and fiber processing. [1] The Master of Science thesis option degree requires students to complete advanced course work and to become skilled in research methodology. [1] Students are expected to plan, conduct and analyze a comprehensive research project, and to report the findings in a thesis, a scholarly document of research conducted in accordance with accepted scientific methodology. [1] The Master of Science non-thesis option degree requires students to complete advanced coursework. [1] Students are not required to complete a final comprehensive exam or report. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological and Agricultural Engineering
Requirements: For admission to full graduate student status in any degree program, the Department requires an overall undergraduate GPA of at least 2.8 based on a 4.0 scale coupled with a 3.0 or higher in the undergraduate major, provided that the major is in an accredited engineering program. [8] Applicants not meeting the requirements for full admission are sometimes granted provisional admission to make up for academic deficiencies. [8] Students not possessing degrees from accredited engineering programs are required to submit GRE scores in Verbal, Quantitative and Analytical Writing. [8]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and College of Engineering
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree in Biological and Agricultural Engineering is pursued by outstanding students with an intense interest in independent study and research. It consists of advanced coursework, a written and oral comprehensive preliminary examination, extended and in-depth research, a written dissertation, and a final oral defense of the research.
ScholarshipType: Graduate research assistantships, teaching assistantships, and fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Biomanufacturing
Requirements: Admission to the master's program, which is referred to as BIOM, requires: Transcripts from an accredited undergraduate degree program in engineering, life science, or physical sciences. A GPA of at least a 3.0 is preferred. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of career goals. A resume. [27]
Description: BTEC offers two graduate degrees: a thesis-basedthemed master's degree (MS) in Biomanufacturing and a Master's degree in Biomanufacturing (MR). Both are Professional Science Master's (PSM) degrees, which provide advanced education in a specific discipline, while simultaneously developing business skills that are highly valued by employers. Both degree programs offer students the option of an upstream (fermentation) or downstream (purification) concentration, as well as courses in global regulatory affairs, protein characterization techniques, cGMP case studies in influenza vaccine manufacturing, case studies in monoclonal antibody production, advanced biomanufacturing and biocatalysis, and an industry internship.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: A BS degree in biomedical engineering or a related field of science or engineering is generally required for admission to the BME Ph.D. program. Applicants with degrees in other fields or from other colleges may be admitted with undergraduate or graduate deficiencies as evaluated by the Graduate Admissions Committee. Students entering at the BME Ph.D. program with an MS degree are expected to have an MS degree in biomedical engineering or a related field of science, medicine, or engineering. In addition to the degree requirement, acceptance to the program will depend on (1) academic excellence, (2) research interests congruent with those of program faculty, and (3) positive recommendations (e.g., from former research advisors).
Description: The Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering Graduate Program is administered by the combined biomedical engineering graduate faculty from both North Carolina State University and University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The joint program also has close working relations with the Research Triangle Institute and industry within the Research Triangle area. These associations enable students to obtain research training in a wide variety of fields and facilitate the selection and performance of dissertation research. Thus, the department, thus, provides students with excellent opportunities to realize the goal of enhancing medical care through the application of modern technology. . [9] Biomedical engineering is a dynamic field stressing the application of engineering techniques and mathematical analysis to biomedical problems. Faculty research programs are key to the program, and they include five primary research directions: rehabilitation engineering, regenerative medicine, biomedical imaging, biomedical microdevices, and pharmacoengineering. [9, 13] The department offers graduate education in biomedical engineering leading to the master of science (MS) and doctor of philosophy (PhD) degrees. [9, 13] Students typically enter this program with backgrounds in engineering, physical science, mathematics or biological science. Curricula are tailored to fit the needs and develop the potential of individual students. In addition, courses in statistics, mathematics, life sciences and engineering provide a well-rounded background of knowledge and skills. [9, 13] A minimum of 52 semester hours of graduate work is required (beyond the Bachelor's degree). Degree candidates in this program are expected to obtain experience working in a research laboratory and to demonstrate proficiency in research. The PhD dissertation should be judged by the graduate committee to be of publishable quality. The student must meet the Graduate School's residency requirement at UNC-CH or NC State as appropriate.

Description: The Ph.D. program in Statistics provides students with comprehensive and rigorous training in cutting-edge statistical theory, methodology, and applications, as well as state-of-the-art computing skills and the ability to conduct high-quality interdisciplinary research. [5] Biostatistics is a key research area within the department, applying statistical methods to biological and health-related data. [9] The department's expertise in biostatistics includes techniques such as Bayesian adaptive trials for designing dynamic clinical studies, reinforcement learning to optimize treatment strategies, causal inference for establishing cause-and-effect relationships, network analysis for understanding complex biological systems, survival data analysis for time-to-event outcomes, nonparametric and functional data methods for analyzing bio-signals from wearables and brain imaging, and longitudinal analysis to track changes in biomarkers over time. The program has been designed for those persons who plan careers in plant operations, design and management. It is not intended to be competitive with the Master of Science degree, which is specifically research oriented, nor with the MBA degree. Rather, the goal of this program is not only to permit earlier productive use of the young engineer's technical skills, but also to a broad concept introduce the engineer to s, analysis, advanced process economics, and technical management. The program is aimed at improving opportunities for chemical engineers in the chemical process industry and related industries. Constituting the program is a core of five (5) required courses plus five elective courses, selected to meet the student's interests in the areas of process control, management and business economics, biochemical and environmental engineering, and petroleum engineering. The courses are available in the late afternoon and evenings, and the degree can be completed in 2-3 years of part-time study. Professionals working in the chemical process industry and related industries with degrees other than but related to chemical engineering (such as mechanical engineering or chemistry) are encouraged to apply. Approximately 54 credit hours are required beyond the M.S. degree or 72 credit hours beyond the B.S. degree. For those with an NC State MS degree in our department, no additional courses are required. For those with an NC State MS degree in another department, 6 credit hours are required in our department. For those with a non NC State MS degree, 12 credit hours of coursework are required. For those with only a Bachelors degree 30 credit hours of coursework are required. The remaining credit hours are research. All Ph.D. students are required to pass a qualifying review before the end of their third semester of study. This review is based on the student's academic performance to date and the results of a project with one of their committee members. Results are presented to the committee in both written and oral form.

[5, 9] When relevant, the applicant must have a score on an English proficiency test equal to or better than Graduate School requirements. [5, 9] A GRE score is not required. Our research and teaching portfolio at North Carolina State University includes food, feed, and fiber crops, turfgrass, and specialty crops. The Crop Science PhD degree program at North Carolina State University emphasizes research and advanced coursework to aid research, and there is also a teaching requirement. After completion of their degrees, our graduate students are in demand. They find diverse employment, including as agricultural consultants; extension agents; golf course managers; postdoctoral scholars; research leaders, managers, or technicians; and faculty members. These positions are found in various sectors including agrochemical and other private sector companies; universities; and government or scientific agencies in the United States and other countries.

[2, 5] Applicants are expected to have mastery in their practice and a clear research topic upon admission. [2, 4] The curriculum comprises a 57-credit, six-semester sequence focused on original design-based investigations. [4]

[3] The program provides students the opportunity to develop and enhance their critical understanding of both the conceptual foundations of parks, recreation and tourism management and the procedures of systematic inquiry and critical problem solving as applied to planning and management issues. [2] It allows each student to develop a plan of study and research that is challenging and stimulating. Description: Established in 1968, the Master of Public Administration (MPA) degree in the Department of Public Administration in the School of Public and International Affairs at NC State remains North Carolina's only MPA available at our state's capitol in Raleigh, NC. [4] We focus on practical and problem-solving skills and emphasize public service values -- including efficiency, effectiveness, equity and accountability. [4] To accomplish this mission, the MPA program offers elective coursework in public management, nonprofit management, urban management, financial management, organizational leadership, public policy and justice administration. [4] The Master of Public Administration program at NC State does not offer formal specializations. [3] Instead, the program affords students the opportunity to tailor individualized public service specialties consistent with their interests and abilities, the university's strengths, and labor market needs. [3]
Accredidation: The MPA Program at NC State is accredited by the NASPAA Commission on Peer Review and Accreditation (COPRA) and is listed on the Annual Roster of Accredited Programs in conformity with NASPAA standards. [3]

Description: The Ph.D. in Soil Science is a research-oriented degree program. It requires a high degree of specialization and expertise in one of the sub-disciplines of soil science. Our goal is to provide M.S. and Ph.D. graduates with the scientific knowledge and professional training they need to address the broad range of environmental and agricultural issues and problems that are related to soils, and to have successful and rewarding careers in the public or private sectors. Students are provided with a fundamental understanding of the biological, chemical and physical properties and processes that are unique to soils. This knowledge is then applied to a diverse field of specializations, ranging from agricultural and environmental applications to the role that soils play in ecosystem structure and function. Our graduates are well-equipped to use their knowledge of soils and their interdisciplinary training to address a wide range of contemporary and emerging issues, such as water quality, waste management, soil and ecosystem remediation, global climate change, and the development of sustainable agricultural systems. Our program provides students with the opportunity to interact with leading scientists in a variety of disciplines, and to conduct research in a state-of-the-art laboratory, greenhouse and field facilities.

Soil science is a rigorous STEM discipline and students accepted will typically have a BS or MS degree in soil science, or closely related fields, with strong preparation in the biological and physical sciences. Description: The Ph.D. program in Statistics is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in universities, as well as in industry and government. Students in the program receive a broad education in the theory and practice of statistics and probability. By the time of graduation, they are well-prepared to make original contributions to the subject. The department is particularly strong in the areas of statistical genetics, environmental and spatial statistics, mathematical statistics and computational statistics; in addition, we have a growing program in machine learning and data science. The department is also known for its strengths in a variety of application areas, including genetics and genomics, environmental sciences, public health and personalized medicine. The department has a long and distinguished record in the training of industrial and academic statisticians and is recognized by the university for its outstanding postdoctoral and graduate programs. There are approximately 80 Ph.D. students in statistics at any one time.

Description:
The Master of Science degree in Statistics is a program of 30 credit hours, which may be completed in one year (fall, spring, summer) or a year and a half. The program is designed to provide a sound statistical foundation for a professional career in industry, government or in the private sector. It can also be a valuable preparation for a Ph.D. program in Statistics or some other field.

The Department of Statistics at NC State is one of the oldest and largest programs in the country. It is a vibrant intellectual community of an internationally recognized faculty and an outstanding student body. Students are admitted to the Statistics Graduate Program either through the Department of Statistics directly or through the Graduate School. A small number of very capable students from other departments at NC State are occasionally admitted as well.

The program is meant to serve practicing high school and college teachers in any discipline that uses data as well as graduate students interested in faculty or teaching careers but can be useful for anyone that presents with data. Those that complete the program should be able to apply common statistical and data science analyses to data using a programming language, understand common misunderstandings in how people interpret data and models, and use data effectively when teaching and presenting.

Submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional for most applicants. Description:
Biochemistry is the science that is dedicated to understanding the molecular basis of life. It is a field with a rich history of discovery and a bright future of even more exciting findings to come. Biochemists are people who ask fundamental questions about the molecular mechanisms that underlie all living processes. What is the molecular nature of a gene? How can a single cell in an embryo develop into the hundreds of different cell types in a mature animal? What is the molecular and cellular basis for memory? How do viruses that have RNA for their genetic material (such as the virus that causes AIDS) replicate that RNA?

Because biochemists are trained to think in the language of both chemistry and biology, they are uniquely poised to unravel the complexities of biological systems. Their interdisciplinary training makes them highly sought-after members of research teams that are composed of scientists from many different disciplines that are working to solve complex biological problems such as the molecular basis of human diseases, the development of new therapeutics, and the production of an adequate and safe food supply. The Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry degree program at NC State provides students with a rigorous training in the fundamental principles of biochemistry, molecular biology, and genetics that will prepare them for a future that is full of discovery.

Description: There are five different avenues to earning a B.S. in Biological Sciences at NC State. Students studying for a degree in Biological Sciences can opt for a general curriculum (BLS) or can choose to focus in a particular area by selecting one of four areas of concentration: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCD), Integrative Physiology and Neurobiology (IPN), Human Biology (HB), or Ecology, Evolution and Conservation Biology (EEC). All new first-year students interested in the B.S. in Biological Sciences start their studies in the NC State Life Sciences First Year Program. The MCD curriculum offers students in-depth studies of the molecular and cellular basis of life and the development of multicellular organisms. The IPN curriculum provides a comprehensive grounding in basic principles of physiology and neuroscience, as well as in-depth exposure to the application of these principles in understanding whole-organism function and the ways in which animals (including humans) cope with challenges presented by their environments. The HB curriculum allows some flexibility for students to study the biology of humans as well as relevant aspects of the humanities and social sciences, while also requiring those science courses most often required by medical schools. A solid education in the scientific and humanistic concepts that underlie modern health sciences and related areas of scientific research is provided. The EEC curriculum offers students in-depth studies in areas of biology at the level of the organism, populations and ecosystems. It is designed for students who have an interest in whole organisms and their biodiversity — what maintains it, what environmental changes affect it, and how to protect it in the face of various challenges.
