Accredidation: The Fisheries concentration meets the qualifications for certification by the American Fisheries Society. [1, 2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology, Wildlife Science Concentration
Requirements: Requirements for first-year applicants include the submission of the Common App, an official high school transcript, and responses to essay prompts. [7] Specifically, applicants must answer, 'Explain why you selected the academic program(s) above and why you are interested in studying these at NC State.' [7] The submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional for applicants who have a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above. [3, 7]
Description: The Fisheries, Wildlife and Conservation Biology (FWCB) major prepares students to manage and conserve populations of fish and wildlife in their natural habitats. This STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) major gives students the skills they need to observe, research, monitor and assess the impact of environmental change, human behavior and public policy on wild populations of animals. Using a combination of lab work, technology and field study, students develop conservation strategies that ensure the long-term health of fish and wildlife populations. After sophomore year, students spend six weeks in summer field courses. During “summer camp” experience, students learn hands-on fish and wildlife management techniques in locations across the state. From plant and animal identification and bird mist nesting netting netting-to-camera-trapping and radio telemetry, students gain experiences that prepare them for careers after graduation. FWCB students have the option to substitute the summer field course with approved internships or study abroad courses. The wildlife concentration provides students with specific coursework necessary to apply for the Associate Wildlife Biologist (AWB) certification from the Wildlife Society upon graduation. The AWB coursework includes extra courses in plant biology, communication, and wildlife habitat management that are not required in the other FWCB concentrations. [2]
Accredidation: The wildlife concentration provides students with specific coursework necessary to apply for the Associate Wildlife Biologist (AWB) certification from The Wildlife Society upon graduation. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Forest Management
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, applicants must submit a complete application through the Common App or the Coalition App. [3] A non-refundable $85 application fee is required, though fee waivers are available. [5] Applicants also need to submit an official high school transcript. [5] NC State's application review considers several factors, including academic achievement, interest in the chosen program, accomplishments outside the classroom, background, and the applicant's individual story. [3]
Description: The forest management, production concentration, trains professionals who will work for forest owners (industrial and individuals) to produce wood fiber and timber, wildlife habitat, and related services forested ecosystems provide. [8, 10] The program of study concentrates attention on the technical planning and economics of forest investments, harvesting, regeneration and operations. [8, 10] Subjects upon which forest management depends include botany, chemistry, ecology, entomology, forest measurements, hydrology, mapping, mathematics, plant physiology, soil science, and statistics. [8, 10] The forest management program includes a nine-week summer practicum between the second and third years of coursework. [8, 10] The purpose of the practicum is to study forest measurement and management skills in the field during concentrated hands-on experiences. [8, 10]
Accredidation: The Society of American Foresters accredits the North Carolina State forest management program. [8, 10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French Language and Literature
Requirements: NC State reviews first-year applications based on academic achievement, including the rigor of the high school curriculum and grades, interest in the intended program of study, and standardized test scores (if submitted). Other factors include accomplishments and involvement outside the classroom, background, and opportunities.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Genetics and Genomics
Requirements: For first-year admission, NC State considers academic achievement, with the most important factor being the applicant's high school transcript. The university conducts a holistic review and also considers factors such as interest in their selected major, extracurricular activities, and background. All applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, an application fee, and self-reported high school grades. A personal essay and a short-answer question about their major are also part of the application.
Description: Die Genetik-Hauptfach ergänzt andere Studiengänge in den biologischen und Lebenswissenschaften an der N.C. State, da es die Studierenden auf weitere Graduiertenstudien, Fachschulen (wie Medizin, Zahnmedizin, Veterinärmedizin, genetische Beratung) oder Karrieren in Branchen vorbereitet, deren Produkte auf biologischer und landwirtschaftlicher Forschung basieren, einschließlich biopharmazeutischer und biotechnologischer Unternehmen. Aufbauend auf der Stärke der NC State als führend in Wissenschaft und Technologie können die Studierenden des Programms problemlos ein begleitendes Nebenfach in einem der anderen lebenswissenschaftlichen Lehrpläne sowie in anderen Programmen wie Statistik oder Biotechnologie erwerben.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Environmental Design in Graphic & Experience Design
Requirements: As a studio-based major, applicants to the Bachelor of Environmental Design in Graphic & Experience Design must submit a 10-piece portfolio and a design essay through their wolfPAW account after submitting the Common Application or Coalition Application.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: NC State considers several factors in its first-year review process, with the most important being academic achievement. This includes the rigor and performance in high school coursework. Beyond academics, the university also considers a student's interest in their chosen program, their background and opportunities, as well as accomplishments and involvement outside the classroom. Things like community service, leadership, and work experience are noted. Applicants are not required to submit an essay or letters of recommendation.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The a Bachelor a of a Arts a in a History a  offers a broad educational experience that also provides essential skills of critical reading, research, judgment, and perspective. [3] These are skills that employers seek in a wide range of fields. [3] The small department offers a “small college” experience within the wealth of NC State's diverse offerings and opportunities. The curriculum offers a great deal of student choice in courses and electives. [3] Flexibility of requirements allows the pursuit of either a diverse experience or a focused, thematic study. [3] Your advisor can help you explore how you might build a thematic interest into your course selection. [3] Examples include our strong course offerings on topics of the law, civil rights and justice, public history, and science and technology in historical context. [3] Beyond traditional courses, there are opportunities for guided and independent research experiences and professional internship. [3] Free electives in the curriculum make it straightforward to complete a Minor in one of the many disciplines at NC State. [3] We offer two specialized tracks within the BA in History: Teacher Education Concentration and the Concentration in Legal History. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science
Requirements: For first-year applicants, North Carolina State University utilizes a holistic review process. Applicants must submit their application via the Common App or Coalition App. The application review considers academic achievement in high school, with an emphasis on rigorous coursework. Submission of ACT or SAT scores is optional for freshman applicants through the fall 2027 term. [47] If a student chooses not to have their test scores considered, no other materials, such as an essay or recommendation, are required in their place. [47] All applicants are required to self-report their high school courses and grades. The application also includes a section for activities and work participation.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: ['Agroecology: Urban Horticulture', 'Plant Breeding & Biotechnology in Horticulture', 'Production Systems and Entrepreneurship in Horticulture', 'Landscape Design, Construction, and Management']
Description: Students learn the methods, processes, art, and science of horticulture. Courses in each concentration vary and are taught in classroom and laboratory settings or, for some classes, online. Internships are required, which provide hands-on experience and learning. Students can follow paths toward industry, entrepreneurship, research, and an advanced degree. [4]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award the associate, baccalaureate, masters and doctorate degrees. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science, Landscape Design, Gardens, and Urban Environments Concentration
Requirements: For admission, first-year applicants must submit a completed Common Application, which includes a personal essay, and self-report their high school courses and grades. There is also a section to provide information about activities and work. Submission of ACT or SAT scores is optional for freshman applicants through the fall 2027 term. [11] While not explicitly listed for this specific program, general undergraduate admissions at NC State do not require a separate resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample beyond the components of the Common Application.
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Landscape Design, Gardens, and Urban Environments Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science offers a concentration in Landscape Design, Gardens, and Urban Environments. This program track is designed for students who want to focus on the art and science of designing, building, and managing landscapes in various settings. The curriculum is menu-driven, allowing students to tailor their studies towards either landscape design or the use of gardens in urban spaces. Students can prepare for careers in residential landscape design, landscape construction and maintenance, public gardens, and urban ecosystem management. The program also provides a foundation for pursuing graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science, Plant Breeding and Applied Genetics Concentration
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit either the Common App or Coalition on Scoir application, a non-refundable $85 application fee (or provide a fee waiver), an official high school transcript, and complete the required essays and short answer questions. [7] The admissions decision is based on a holistic review of the student's high school academic record, interest in their chosen program, extracurricular involvement, and other factors. [10] Submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional for applicants with a weighted high school GPA of 2.8 or above. [7]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Concentration: Plant Breeding and Biotechnology in Horticulture Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science: Plant Breeding & Biotechnology in Horticulture Concentration is one of the four concentrations offered in by the Department of Horticultural Science. [3] Students are offered a unique look at various aspects of Horticulture. The Plant Breeding & Biotechnology in Horticulture concentration is a menu driven concentration that allows students to direct their education in either plant breeding or biotechnology. [2] Students are required to take two Biology courses, Soil Science, General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry I and II, Biochemistry, Genetics, and Whole Plant Physiology. [2] The remaining courses for the major are selected from a series of topical menus: Plant Protection Electives, Business Electives, and Advised Electives. [2] Students can follow paths toward research and biotechnology in academia or industry or pursue a graduate degree. [2]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctorate degrees. [6] Information on specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science program by a professional association is not available on the university's accreditation page.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science, Production Systems and Entrepreneurship in Horticulture Concentration
Requirements: Considerations for admission include academic success (GPA and SAT or ACT scores) as well as extracurricular activities like leadership and community service experience.
Concentration: Production Systems and Entrepreneurship in Horticulture Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science: Production Systems and Entrepreneurship in Horticulture Concentration is one of the four concentrations offered in by the Department of Horticultural Science. Students are offered a unique look at various aspects of Horticulture. [1] The Production Systems and Entrepreneurship in Horticulture Concentration concentration is a menu driven concentration that allows students to direct their education in either ornamental or edible plant production. [1] Students are required to take two Biology courses, Soil Science, General Chemistry, Introduction to Organic Chemistry, Whole Plant Physiology, and a lower level Genetics. [1] The remaining courses for the major are selected from a series of topical menus: Plant Protection Electives, Business Electives, and Advised Electives. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticultural Science, Science and Technology of Horticultural Crops Concentration
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a non-refundable application fee, and self-reported high school courses and grades. A personal essay is a required part of the application. Submission of ACT/SAT scores is optional for freshman applicants through the fall 2027 term. A resume and a separate writing sample are not required for general first-year admission.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Biology
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences with a Human Biology Concentration at North Carolina State University, prospective students must follow the general first-year application process. All new first-year students interested in this program begin their studies in the NC State Life Sciences First Year Program. The application is submitted through the Common Application or Coalition Application. There are no specific requirements for a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample for admission to this program beyond the standard application essays. [10, 11]
Description:
The bachelor of science (BS) degree in biological sciences educates students broadly in biology. As a BS biological sciences student, you'll explore the structure, function, behavior arid evoluation fells, organisma, populations and ecosystems. Students seeking a degree in biological sciences can opt for a general curriculum (BLS) or focus on a particular area by selecting one of our four concentrations. All these programs lead to a variety of overlapping postgraduation academic and career options; we encourage you to look at the differences in course requirements and select the curriculum that best matches your academic interests. Students in all of these programs take the same core courses in introductory biology, chemistry, physics and calculus, and they must meet the same general education requirements. The curricula differ in more advanced course requirements and electives.

The human biology (HB) concentration offers training in areas of science important to health-related professions, as well as relevant aspects of the humanities and social sciences. Students in the HB concentration get a solid education in the scientific and humanistic concepts that underlie modern health sciences and related areas of scientific research. This curriculum allows students to complete health care professional program prerequisites. In HB concentration courses, you can explore upper-level sciences as well as health care economics, ethics, advancements in applied problem solving and other issues related to human health.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Industrial Design
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Industrial Design, a studio-based major, first-year applicants must submit a completed Common Application or Coalition Application by the November 1st deadline, listing a studio-based major as their first choice. A second choice major, which cannot be another studio-based major, is strongly suggested. In addition to the main application, applicants must submit a 10-piece digital portfolio and a design-specific essay through their wolfPAW account. [7] The portfolio should consist of 10 separate images of the applicant's creative work and can include various mediums such as two-dimensional design (drawing, painting), three-dimensional design (sculpture, furniture), and digital media. [7] The pieces do not have to be specific to the industrial design discipline. [7] The required design essay for Industrial Design applicants has a specific prompt: "Discuss one project in your portfolio that best reflects your current understanding of design. Consider how it might be received or used by somebody other than yourself." The response should be between 250-300 words. [5]
Description: Industrial The Industrial Design Program offers a four-year professional bachelor degree. [4] Design is concerned with all human aspects of products/technologies/systems and their relationship to people. The industrial designer is responsible for product safety, aesthetics, usability, maintenance, and cost. [4] Industrial designers deal with consumer and industrial products. [4] In order to achieve these ends, designers must be involved in major design and research areas such as human behavior, human-machine relationships, the environment, and the product itself. In addition, the designer's responsibility extends into sustainability, product liability, and cross-cultural issues. [4] The goal of the Industrial Design curriculum is to teach the design and development of products or product systems and their relationship to human beings and the environment. [4] The study of Industrial Design at NC State University is a four-year (eight-semester) program that awards a professional Bachelor of Industrial Design (BID) degree after the fulfillment of all academic requirements. [3] The curriculum emphasizes developing students' skills in design research, conceptualization, prototyping, and production, preparing them to address real-world challenges across various industries. [5]
Accredidation: The program offers Bachelor of Industrial Design (BID) and Master of Industrial Design (MID) degrees, both accredited by The National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, applicants must submit an application through the Common App or Coalition on Scoir, pay a non-refundable application fee, and submit an official high school transcript. Students must select a major on their application. Your choice of major is a factor in the admission review process.
Description: Industrial engineering is a branch of engineering that focuses on optimizing complex processes, systems, and organizations by improving efficiency, productivity, and quality. It combines principles from engineering, mathematics, and business to design, analyze, and manage systems that involve people, materials, information, equipment, and energy. Industrial engineers aim to reduce waste, streamline operations, and enhance overall performance across various industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and service sectors.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
MaxFails: Students must successfully complete at least 2/3 of all attempted credit hours to maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress. [18, 21]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
Requirements: Admission to NC State is highly competitive and is based on a holistic review of a complete application. Of primary importance is the student's academic record, including the level and difficulty of courses taken and the overall grade point average. [7] Other factors considered include interest in the chosen major, accomplishments outside the classroom, background, and the applicant's individual story. [5, 7] Admission to the Interdisciplinary Studies Self-Design Major program is by a separate application after enrollment at NCSU and requires the student to identify a faculty sponsor to develop an academically sound major. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
Requirements: Prospective students apply for undergraduate admission to North Carolina State University. The Bachelor of Arts in International Studies is a program within the School of Public and International Affairs in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. General application requirements include a review of the student's high school record. While not a formal statement of purpose, applicants must respond to short-answer questions. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Leadership and Professional Practice
Requirements: To be admitted to the LPS distance education degree completion program, a competitive candidate must have: An Associate of Arts degree (A.A.) or Associate of Science degree (A.S.) from the last 15 years or approximately 60 university credit hours of college-level work including a significant amount of social science courses. (A maximum of 70 credit hours can transfer into the LPS program.) A 3.0 GPA on your completed approved college-level work. However, emphasis will be placed on the most recent academic coursework completed. A college-level English course (4 hours); A college-level math course (3 hours); A complete application form.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Leadership in the Public Sector
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Leadership in the Public Sector is a degree-completion program designed for students who have already completed some college coursework. Competitive candidates for admission are expected to have an Associate of Arts (A.A.) or Associate of Science (A.S.) degree, or approximately 60 transferable credit hours. A cumulative GPA of 3.0 on completed college-level work is considered competitive, with an emphasis placed on the most recent coursework. Applicants should have also completed a college-level English course (4 hours) and a college-level math course (3 hours). [9]
Concentration: ['Leadership in Security', 'Leadership in Nonprofit Sector', 'Public Affairs Leadership']
Description: The B.A. in Leadership in the Public Sector is a degree-completion program designed for students who have already completed some college coursework, and is ideal for community college transfers, military personnel and their families, and other adult learners. It is a fully online undergraduate program, meaning that all necessary courses are available through distance learning, offering flexibility to complete the bachelor's degree at one's own pace. The program provides a liberal arts foundation in the ethical, theoretical, and policy analytical skills necessary to be effective leaders in public and nonprofit sector organizations. Graduates pursue careers in public and nonprofit organizations, as well as with private firms, and many seek advanced degrees in political science, public administration, nonprofit sector management, and law. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: To apply as a first-year applicant, candidates must submit either the Common App or the Coalition on Scoir application. A non-refundable application fee of $85 is required, though fee waivers are available. On the application, students will select a first and second choice major. NC State looks for strong academic achievement, including competitive grades and challenging courses like honors, AP, IB, or dual enrollment. Applicants should aim to meet the minimum course requirements set by the UNC System. While not explicitly required for general admission, letters of recommendation are considered if submitted.
Description: At NC State, Materials Science and Engineering students are trained to understand the complexities of all classes of material. Our curriculum begins with core courses in thermodynamics, kinetics, and structure, building a strong foundation before advancing to mechanical, thermal, electrical, magnetic, and optical properties. Hands-on learning is a cornerstone of the program, with two laboratory courses that immerse students in analytical techniques to characterize materials at all scales and measure their properties. Our program covers cutting-edge technologies like nanomaterials, biomaterials, advanced functional materials, materials forensics, computational modeling, and AI-driven materials optimization. With five technical electives, students can tailor their education with courses in materials processing, engineering, chemistry, physics, mathematics, statistics, biological sciences, computer science, data science, and beyond. This flexibility allows students to prepare for diverse career paths in industry or pursue graduate studies. In our two-semester capstone senior design project, students apply their knowledge to solve practical materials challenges with industry partners. Working in teams, you'll tackle hands-on problems and bridge classroom learning with real-world impact.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering, Biomaterials Concentration
Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering, Nanomaterials Concentration
Requirements: Initial admission is not directly to the Nanomaterials concentration. Students must first complete the standard set of first-year engineering courses. After completing these courses, students can apply to join the Department of Materials Science and Engineering and declare the nanomaterials concentration through the CODA (Change of Degree Application) process. [2, 7] For general first-year admission to the university, NC State will consider factors such as grades, course curriculum, interest in the applied program, background, and accomplishments. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: NC State is test optional for first-year applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above. [11] Prospective students who plan to apply with a weighted GPA greater than or equal to 2.5 and less than 2.8 will be required to submit a standardized test score of a 17 or higher on the ACT, or a 930 or higher on the SAT, with your application. [11] If you have a weighted GPA of 2.8 or higher, no additional application materials are required if you opt not to submit your test scores. [11]
Description: The heart of the program consists of fundamental courses in the main areas of mathematics (numerical analysis, algebra, analysis), together with a variety of specialized, elective courses. It is complemented by supportive courses from other departments, in addition to the University general education requirements. [3] Opportunities for internship and research are given, preparing students for the job market and for higher studies. [3] With a pedagogy emphasizing students' learning outcomes and encouraging the use of technology, students are aided in developing quantitative skills and an ability to think clearly and critically about complex problems, while communicating results with precision. [3]
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctorate degrees. [12, 13] The official North Carolina State University website does not mention a specific programmatic accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to NC State is highly competitive and based on a holistic review. Primary factors include a student's high school academic record, including the difficulty of courses, GPA, and class rank. The application review also considers interest in the chosen program, accomplishments outside the classroom, background, and individual story. [4] Applicants must complete an application via the Common App or Coalition App, pay an $85 fee (or use a fee waiver), and submit an official high school transcript. [6]
Description: The Mechanical Engineering degree program prepares its graduates for careers in mechanical and thermal systems design, analysis and manufacturing. Mechanical engineering involves practical application of mechanical and thermal sciences to research, design, development, testing and manufacturing of a wide variety of products. Mechanical engineers contribute to the fields of transportation, power generation and energy conversion, environmental control and pollution abatement, noise control, and biomechanics. Recent developments have increased interest in such areas as robotics, mechatronics, precision engineering, automated manufacturing systems, combustion and propulsion.
Accredidation: The NC State Mechanical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechatronics Engineering
Description: The Joint NC State/UNC Asheville claustru Mechaunisce tronicilor (JEM) combină cele mai bune oferte de la două universități recunoscute la nivel național. De la Universitatea de Stat din NC vine componenta de inginerie care cuprinde cursuri de la Departamentele de Inginerie Mecanică și Aerospațială (MAE), Inginerie Electrică și Informatică (ECE) și cursuri de mecatronică predate de facultatea Universității de Stat din NC în campusul Universității din Carolina de Nord Asheville. De la UNC Asheville vine o componentă de Științe Umaniste și Științe Sociale cu o bază bogată în arte liberale și cursuri de mecatronică predate de personalul UNC Asheville. Laboratoarele practice sunt parte integrantă a cursurilor de inginerie. Fiind un program de inginerie bazat pe site-ul NC State, studenții trebuie să participe la cursuri în campusul UNC Asheville. [5]
Accredidation: The Joint BS in Engineering - Mechatronics Concentration degree is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Meteorology
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, applicants must submit either the Common App or the Coalition on Scoir application, and pay a non-refundable $85 application fee. [7, 9] Applicants are asked to select up to two majors on their application. [7] The admissions decision is based on a holistic review which primarily considers the student's high school academic achievement, including the rigor of courses and GPA. [9] Other factors include interest in the chosen program, accomplishments outside the classroom, background, and individual story. [9]
Description: The degree of Bachelor of Science in Meteorology is offered in the Department of Marine, Earth and Atmospheric Sciences. A concentration in Marine Science may also be chosen. Meteorologists study a diverse array of topics, including climate, air pollution, environmental impacts, weather analysis and forecasting, remote sensing, atmospheric physics and interactions between the atmosphere and other components of the earth system. [6]
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the undergraduate cost per credit hour is $272.29 for in-state students and $1,312.50 for out-of-state students. [7, 5]
MaxFails: Students with a cumulative GPA less than 2.0 and a grade point deficit greater than 15 at the end of any term will be placed on Academic Suspension. [20]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarship awards can range from $500 to $10,000 per year. [35]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships can be awarded on the basis of financial need, merit or both. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students at North Carolina State University are not specific to the Bachelor of Science in Microbiology program. All applicants apply through the Common App or the Coalition App. The application includes questions about the applicant's background, their family, and their academic and extracurricular activities. Applicants must also submit a personal essay. While not explicitly required for all majors, some programs may have additional requirements or recommendations, but none are specified for Microbiology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology, Microbial Biotechnology Concentration
Requirements: Application requirements are not specified at the individual program level for undergraduate studies. Prospective students should follow the general first-year or transfer application requirements provided by the Office of Undergraduate Admissions.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Microbiology program at North Carolina State University provides a comprehensive understanding of microscopic, generally single-celled, organisms and viruses, including their growth, development, physiology, classification, ecology, and genetics. These organisms often serve as model systems for understanding fundamental processes common to all living cells, and many major discoveries in biology and genomic science have resulted from studying them. The program emphasizes that future advancements in biotechnology, food and fuel production, and human and animal health are heavily dependent on understanding microbial processes. Students have the option to pursue a general microbiology curriculum or specialize in one of three concentrations that align with common career paths: Microbial Biotechnology, Microbial Research, or Microbial Health Sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology, Microbial Health Sciences Concentration
Requirements: NC State conducts a holistic review of a student's application, considering their academic achievement, including the rigor of their high school curriculum. Other factors considered are a student's interest in their chosen program, accomplishments and involvement outside the classroom, and their background and opportunities. The Common Application, including the personal essay, is required.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Microbiology is concerned with the growth and development, physiology, classification, ecology, genetics, and other aspects of the life process of an array of microscopic, generally single-celled, organisms and viruses. [7, 9] These organisms frequently serve as model systems for elucidation of fundamental processes that are common to all living cells. [7, 9] Most of the major discoveries that have produced spectacular advances in biology and genomic science during the past decade have resulted from studies of microbial systems. [7, 9] Future developments in biotechnology, production of food and fuel, and human and animal health will rely heavily on understanding microbial processes. [7] There are 4 avenues to earning a B.S. in Microbiology. [7, 9] Students can opt for a general curriculum (MBIO) or can choose to focus in a particular area by selecting one of three areas of concentration: Microbial Biotechnology (MBIO-MT) or Microbial Research (MBIO-MR) or Microbial Health Sciences (MBIO-HS). [7, 9] These concentrations mirror the three most common career paths of Microbiology majors: work in research laboratories and production facilities, further study in graduate school (at the Masters or Doctoral level), and further study in professional schools such as medical and dental schools. [7, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology, Microbial Research Concentration
Requirements: NC State reviews first-year applications for admission based on a combination of factors, including academic performance (GPA and course rigor), interest in the chosen academic program, background and opportunities, and accomplishments outside the classroom. The application requires responses to short answer questions. A resume is not listed as a required or recommended item for first-year applicants.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Middle Grades English Language Arts and Social Studies Education
Requirements: NC State requires that all applicants for undergraduate admission be a graduate of a regionally accredited high school or a non-public high school that is registered with the N.C. Department of Non-Public Education and that they meet the minimum course requirements as established by the UNC Board of Governors. Beyond these minimums, the university considers a number of factors in its admission decision. These factors include the student's academic record in high school, class rank, standardized test scores (although scores are not required for students applying for admission through fall 2024), extracurricular activities, and an essay. For transfer students, the most important factor is their academic record at the institution(s) from which they are transferring.
Description: The MSL Program offers an undergraduate degree and initial licensure in two dynamic content areas that prepares teachers to effectively educate and impact the lives of young adolescents while being responsive to their unique needs, interests, and abilities. Students learn how to implement high-quality English language arts and social studies instruction with three major focus areas: digital literacies, inquiry-based learning, and citizenship.
Accredidation: North Carolina State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctorate degrees. [3] The program is also accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Middle Grades Mathematics and Science Education
Requirements: Admission to North Carolina State University is based on a holistic review of an applicant's academic record, standardized test scores (if submitted), and other supporting documents. Specific requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Middle Grades Mathematics and Science Education program are not explicitly detailed on the university's website, as the program appears to be offered as separate concentrations in Mathematics and Science.
Description: The Mathematics Education: Middle Grades Concentration (BS) degree is one of four undergraduate degree options in the Mathematics Education program in the Department of STEM Education. This degree program prepares teacher-leaders to have a deep understanding of the mathematics and statistics they will teach and knowledge about different pedagogical strategies they can apply in the classroom. Students take five courses focused on mathematics education, beginning in their sophomore year. In addition, students take courses specific to teaching content in the middle grades. Our professional courses in the junior and senior year offer relevant pedagogical experiences, emphasize teaching mathematics with technology, and provide rich field experiences in math classrooms. Graduates are recommended for an initial North Carolina teaching license in mathematics grades 6-9. Students in this program have the option to pursue a dual teaching license. This means they will receive a BS in Mathematics Education but they may be recommended for licensure in both middle grades mathematics and middle grades science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources
Requirements: Prospective first-year students must submit an application and will be evaluated on academic achievement, including grades and curriculum rigor. Other factors considered are interest in the intended program, background, opportunities, and extracurricular accomplishments. For transfer students, primary consideration is given to the cumulative GPA from all previously attended institutions and the number of credit hours completed.
Fees: The annual undergraduate rate is $6,535 for North Carolina residents and $31,500 for nonresidents. [35]
Concentration: ['Ecosystem Assessment Concentration', 'Policy and Administration Concentration', 'Soil, Water and Land Use Concentration']
Description: Undergraduate programs in forestry and environmental resources incorporate the many topics needed to make decisions about how society will interact with natural resources, including the aquatic, atmospheric, and terrestrial ecosystems upon which human lives depend. [2] Faculty and students in the Department of Forestry and Environmental Resources study all of these resources and their interactions. [2] As they plan for and assess impacts to natural resources, they integrate STEM and social science areas of study in multiple ways. [2] All of our students graduate with a wealth of real-world experiences and a deep understanding of the interdisciplinary nature of solving complex challenges. [2] The Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources degree with a concentration in Soil, Water, and Land Use encompasses the study of soil, water, air, minerals, flora, fauna and people. [9] In this degree, students acquire a solid foundation in resource management with a focus on soil properties and surface and groundwater hydrology. [9]
Accredidation: The Natural Resources program is fully accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF). [3, 10]
CostPerCredit: Undergraduates will be charged $62.50 per credit hour for the COE Program Enhancement Fee. [18]
ScholarshipAmount: Academic Scholarships in the Department of Forestry and Environmental Resources usually provide $4,000 - $6,000 per year. College-wide scholarships typically range from $500-$2,500. [31, 10]
ScholarshipType: Academic Scholarship, Summer Camp Scholarships and Work Scholarships. [31]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources, Ecosystem Assessment Concentration
Requirements: First-year applicants must apply using the Common Application. Required materials include the application, a self-reported academic record, and a recommendation from a school counselor. While not required, applicants can have one teacher or other mentor submit a letter of recommendation. NC State is test-optional, so applicants can choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores.
Description: TwoFuse-produced curricula in natural resources are offered by the Department of Forestry and Environmental Resources. These curricula hold accreditation from the Society of American Foresters, equipping natural resources professionals with a wide-ranging interdisciplinary background and the focused skills necessary for managing natural resources. The Natural Resources curricula share a common set of courses designed to emphasize the integrated approach required in interdisciplinary teamwork. The curriculum for Natural Resources Ecosystem Assessment is designed to produce graduates who are knowledgeable and skilled in inventorying and describing the characteristics of ecosystems, as well as in evaluating the effects of management decisions. [1] A critical component of development planning, ecosystem assessment or environmental impact assessment, requires individuals who have a deep understanding of ecosystem structure and processes. These individuals must be capable of identifying, measuring, inventorying, and describing ecosystems, and applying standard evaluation and classification systems, such as wildlife habitat evaluation procedures and the federal criteria for wetland delineation. The curriculum is built on a strong scientific foundation and includes advanced courses in sampling and measurement techniques, vegetation, soils, hydrology, and wildlife and fisheries. The 400-level courses further explore the techniques and issues of natural resource management. [1]
Accredidation: The curricula are also accredited by the Society of American Foresters and produce natural resources professionals with a broad interdisciplinary background coupled with specifically focused skills needed to manage natural resources. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources, Marine and Coastal Resources Concentration
Requirements: NC State is test-optional for first-year applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or higher. For these students, the submission of SAT or ACT scores is not required, and they will not be disadvantaged if they choose not to submit them. [8] Prospective students with a weighted GPA between 2.5 and less than 2.8 are required to submit a standardized test score of 17 or higher on the ACT or 930 or higher on the SAT. [8] All applicants must submit their application via the Common Application or the Coalition on Scoir Application. A personal essay is a required part of the application.
Description: The degree of Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources is available with a concentration in Marine and Coastal Resources. [1] Marine scientists explore all aspects of the seas and coastal regions, seeking to understand how the oceans, their biological communities, the solid earth and the atmosphere interact. [1, 2] As professionals with interdisciplinary training, marine scientists are needed to advise business, industry and governments on the potential impact of human activities and the wise use of marine resources. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources, Policy and Administration Concentration
Requirements: Given the diverse range of programs and applicant types, North Carolina State University does not specify a single set of general application requirements at the institutional level. Application requirements are detailed separately for undergraduate and graduate programs, and often vary further by the specific program of interest.
Description: Two aresources are curriculaoffered Forestry and Environmental Resources. The curricula are also accredited by the Society of American Foresters and produce natural resources professionals with a broad interdisciplinary background coupled with specifically focused skills needed to manage natural resources. The Natural Resources curricula include a series of common courses to highlight the integrated nature of work by interdisciplinary teams. The curriculum in Natural Resources Ecosystem Assessment produces graduates who have knowledge and skills to inventory and describe ecosystems characteristics and to evaluate the impacts of management decisions. Ecosystem assessment or environmental impact assessment is an important part of development planning that calls for individuals who understand ecosystem structure and processes; who can identify, measure, inventory, and describe ecosystems; and who can apply standard evaluation and classification systems such as wildlife habitat evaluation procedures and the federal wetland delineation criteria. The curriculum entails a strong science base, as well as advanced courses in sampling and measurements, vegetation, soils, hydrology, and wildlife and fisheries are added. The 400-level courses also address techniques and issues of natural resource management. The curriculum in Natural Resources Policy and Administration produces graduates who have knowledge and skills to manage natural resources programs in a variety of settings and organizations with an emphasis on public agencies. The advanced courses of the curriculum provide background in economics, policy, government, public administration, and natural resources management. An economics track begins with introductory microeconomics and culminates with environmental economics and public finance. Courses in government and public administration provide knowledge of how public institutions work. Courses in forestry, wildlife and fisheries, parks and recreation management, and geographic information systems address specific topics of resource management and provide opportunities for students to develop skills and knowledge in their interest area.
Accredidation: The curricula are also accredited by the Society of American Foresters and produce natural resources professionals with a broad interdisciplinary background coupled with specifically focused skills needed to manage natural resources. [1]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [2]

The application is reviewed based on a holistic process that considers academic performance, extracurricular activities, and other personal attributes.

Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nutrition Science prepares graduates for a career in healthcare or community nutrition education and emphasizes: Health, wellness, and lifestyle habits related to food choices; Nutrients required by the body, their food source, functions, deficiencies and toxicities; Evidence-based medical nutrition therapy practices for disease prevention and treatment. [1] This degree has two different concentration areas requiring 42 general credit hours and a 41-hour required program core. [1] The Dietetics concentration is an Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) accredited Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) program. [1] This program prepares highly qualified graduates for supervised practice leading to eligibility for the CDR credentialing exam to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDN). [1] The Food and Nutrition concentration incorporates food, nutrition, life science, public health, social science and social work courses to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to educate various populations in the area of health and wellness. [1]
Accredidation: The Dietetics concentration is an Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) accredited Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) program. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition Science, Applied Nutrition Concentration
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students include the completed Common Application or Coalition Application, a non-refundable application fee, and self-reported high school grades. Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutrition Science, Nutrition with Science Concentration
Description: The Nutrition Science Bachelor of Science degree has two sub-plans to choose from: the Science track or the Applied track. The Science curriculum is designed for those students with an interest in graduate school or post-graduate training in a human health profession for which physics and 4 semesters of chemistry are required.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Paper Science and Engineering
Requirements: NC State is test-optional for first-year applicants with a weighted high school GPA of 2.8 or higher. For these students, the submission of SAT/ACT scores is their choice. Prospective students applying with a weighted GPA between 2.5 and less than 2.8 are required to submit a standardized test score. [12] The SAT Essay or ACT Writing section is not required. [12]
Description: Science, engineering, and mathematics form the basis for a multidisciplinary approach to understanding the fundamental aspects of materials science and engineering of these complex renewable materials. [1, 4] The Paper Science and Engineering curriculum prepares students for careers in the paper industry, which ranks as the fifth-largest manufacturing industry in the United States. [1, 4] Students study the technology and engineering of wood pulping processes, chemical and energy recovery systems, and pulp bleaching. [1, 4] In addition, various papermaking operations, such as refining, sizing, coating, and drying are studied. [1, 4] These topics, along with the chemical and biological modification of wood, papermaking, and the physics of paper based materials form a fundamental set of core courses that all students in the curriculum take. [1, 4] Two concentrations are available emphasizing the different engineering aspects of pulping and paper making. [1, 4] The Paper Science and Engineering concentration provides an extensive background in the pulp and paper manufacturing processes and elective credit hours for studies in chemistry, marketing, economics, management or other areas of interest to the student. [1, 4] Greater depth in general chemical engineering principles can be obtained from the Chemical Engineering Concentration. [1, 4] Students who have completed the Chemical Engineering Concentration in Paper Science and Engineering can, in cooperation with the College of Engineering and with an additional semester of study, earn a Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering as a second degree. [1, 4]
Accredidation: The Paper Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. [1, 5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management

Description: In today's fast-paced society, recreation and leisure are more important than ever to our physical and mental well-being. Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management (PRTM) students learn to create and facilitate sustainable and affordable experiences in local and global communities bv utilitizing guest best business practices in programming, marketing and budgeting. Our students graduate prepared to make a difference in people's lives by creating quality recreation and nature-based programs, education and events that provide leisure, enhance community and address societal concerns-such as physical health, juvenile delinquency and economic sustainability. Our students gain real-world experience through hands-on classes and internships. Students benefit from partnerships with local and state agencies, nonprofits and a network of parks in the greater Raleigh area. Our college is home to the NC State Tourism Extension Office, which is committed to boosting economic and community development efforts in rural North Carolina. Our students have the opportunity to gain professional and leadership experience by assisting this office with projects in the areas of agri-tourism and micro-entrepreneurship.
Accredidation: The Parks, Recreation, and Tourism Management baccalaureate degree program is accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions (COAPRT). [2]

ScholarshipType: Academic merit and leadership, with financial need also considered. [2]

[5, 7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management, Program Management Concentration
Requirements: For undergraduate first-year applicants, North Carolina State University requires the submission of a completed Common App or Coalition App, an $85 application fee or fee waiver, and an official high school transcript. Description: The Bachelor of Science in Parks, Recreation, and Tourism Management with a Program Management concentration at North Carolina State University provides students with a comprehensive education to prepare them for leadership roles in the fields of parks, recreation, and tourism. The program focuses on developing the necessary skills for managing various recreational facilities, tourism enterprises, and community recreation programs. It establishes a strong foundation in recreation management principles, including planning, marketing, budgeting, and leadership, complemented by specialized coursework in program management. Students delve into subjects like facility operations, event planning, customer service, risk management, and sustainable tourism practices. Practical experience is integrated through internships, service-learning projects, and collaborations with industry partners.
Accredidation: The curriculum in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management is a professional program accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management, Sustainable Tourism and Hospitality Management Concentration
Description: Tourism and Event Management students seek opportunities to work with people; think strategically and enjoy the process of planning; are inspired by the world's unique natural and cultural resources; and want to use travel and events to bring people closer together. Examples of concentration courses include: Sustainable Tourism; Destination Planning and Management; Services, Facilities, and Event Marketing; Tourism, Poverty, and Health; and Special Event Planning. [5] The curriculum in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management is a professional program...The curriculum provides students with a broad education in natural sciences, humanities, and social sciences, and fosters the professional, technical, and communication skills needed to plan and implement recreation programs and tourism events, manage parks and facilities, and design tourism services. [5] The curriculum is designed to prepare students for a variety of positions in a dynamic, people-centered profession that includes some of the fastest growing sectors of the global economy. The curriculum provides 42 hours of core coursework that includes foundations of tourism and event management, geospatial problem solving, outdoor recreation management, organizational leadership, fiscal management, and recreation programming. [5]
Accredidation: The curriculum in Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management is a professional program accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions. [5]

Description: The Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Philosophy, and a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Philosophy, plus three concentrations. These different programs all cover basic core areas of philosophy that are essential to any good philosophy major, but they also allow students to pursue and showcase different areas of emphasis. The biggest differences between the B.A. in Philosophy and the B.S. in Philosophy arise from differences between the College of Humanities and Social Sciences' requirements for the B.A. and the B.S. These differences can be summarized as follows: For the B.A., the College requires more courses in the humanities and social sciences, including a 3-credit 201-level course in a foreign language. The B.A. in Philosophy is, in general, best suited to: Students with strong interests in a world language, history or literature; Students who would like to transfer to a philosophy major from another major in the humanities or social sciences; Students who would like to combine a major in philosophy with another major in the humanities or social sciences. [13, 10]

Description: The Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Philosophy, and a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Philosophy, plus three concentrations. The B.S. in Philosophy with a Concentration in Logic, Representation and Reasoning provides excellent preparation for top graduate programs in Philosophy as well as for professional training in fields as diverse as law, library science, management and medicine. [3, 5] Although the major does not train students for a particular career, it develops skills that are useful for work in any field that requires critical, constructive and independent thinking. [3, 5]

In the modern world, physicists often interact with a large number of other disciplines to address pressing academic and applied problems. Most physics majors find employment in a government or industrial laboratory, or with a company that provides STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) products or services. Other physics majors go on to graduate studies in physics or related sciences, or professional schools (such as medicine or law).  The Interdisciplinary Physics Concentration at NC State allows students to customize a highly technical Bachelor of Science degree in consultation with an expert Faculty advisor. [6] The combinations of different scientific fields that can be incorporated into the Interdisciplinary concentration are almost limitless. Examples include biophysics, geophysics, mathematical physics, and data science. [6, 8]

Applicants must apply for first-year admission to the university. This process includes completing an online application, submitting a high school transcript, and an application fee. NC State reviews applicants based on academic achievement in high school, including the rigor of the curriculum, class rank, and GPA. Other factors considered are interest in the intended major, extracurricular activities, and accomplishments.

an emphasis on animals. Required courses are designed to develop breadth and depth in core areas, providing a strong base for all Zoology majors. Students acquire a knowledge of zoology from the organizational level of molecules and cells to the organizational level of ecosystems, with flexibility in the selection of upper level courses to specialize or remain generalized, according to individual interests and career goals. Core courses provide a foundation for all students in writing and communication, math and statistical sciences, natural sciences, natural history, and the human dimensions of conservation and natural resource management. Zoology electives are chosen with guidance from professional and faculty advisors. These electives in combination with additional science and math electives allow students to explore more advanced topics ranging from behavior, ecology, and climate science to data science and geographic information systems. All Zoology majors must complete an Experiential Learning Experience. This high-impact experience gives students real world experience through internships, volunteering, research, or teaching positions.

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Description: Students completing a Minor in Accounting will: Be familiar with the areas of financial accounting, managerial accounting, and other accounting topics. Understand that accounting is an information system for measuring, processing, and communicating financial information about economic entities. Understand how accounting information allows users to make reasoned choices among alternative uses of scarce resources in the conduct of business and economic activities.

ProgramName: Minor in Africana Studies
Requirements: Students can apply for admission to any university minor program in MyPack Portal. Admission will be based on the student's academic record, and in most cases no longer requires departmental review. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Agribusiness Management
Requirements: Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better and the completion of ARE 201 Introduction to Agricultural & Resource Economics or EC 201 Principles of Microeconomics with a grade of C- or better. [3, 9] Students should contact Dr. John S. Russ, to inquire about adding the minor no later than the registration period for the student's final semester at NC State. [3]
Description: The minor in Agricultural Business Management is offered to undergraduate majors in all departments except the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics. The minor provides students an opportunity to learn basic business and economic principles that are useful in careers in agricultural and related industries. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Agricultural Business Management
Requirements: Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better and the completion of ARE 201 Introduction to Agricultural & Resource Economics or EC 201 Principles of Microeconomics with a grade of C- or better. [2]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The minor in Agricultural Business Management is offered to undergraduate majors in all departments except the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics. The minor provides students an opportunity to learn basic business and economic principles that are useful in careers in agricultural and related industries.
ScholarshipType: The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) offers various scholarships. While specific types for this minor aren't detailed, university scholarships are generally merit-based, need-based, and identity-based.

ProgramName: Minor in Agroecology
Requirements: Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better. A minimum of 17 hours is required for the minor in Agroecology. Students are required to complete 11 credits of required courses and a minimum of 6 credits of restricted elective courses. A minimum grade of 'C-' or better is required in each course selected. No courses for the minor may be taken using the S/U option. Students majoring in Agroecology and Sustainable Food Systems (11ASFSBS), Crop and Soil Sciences (11CSSCBS), and Natural Resources - Soil, Water and Land Use (11NATRLBS) are not eligible to enroll in this minor. [1]
Description: The minor in Agroecology is open to all undergraduate students at NC State University. It is designed for students majoring in the biological sciences, agronomy, horticulture and animal sciences, but will be of interest seasonings wide away students have brought them vacations in the life sciences, economics, and sociology. Agroecology instruction provides students a fundamental understanding of agriculture and its interaction with natural and social systems. Students selecting the Agroecology minor will gain an understanding of modern production agriculture from an ecological and sociological perspective, obtain new skills in analyzing agricultural systems, and the knowledge to design a plan for change. This knowledge will improve a student's ability to work with agricultural professionals to implement a system that meets ecological and social needs while remaining profitable for farmers. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Animal Science
Requirements: The Department of Animal Science offers an undergraduate minor in Animal Science to all interested baccalaureate students. [5] Students who plan to minor in Animal Science should complete ANS 150 and then apply to add the minor in MyPack's Change of Degree Application (CODA). [3, 5] A minimum of 15 credit hours is required, and students must maintain a grade of 'C-' or higher in each course. [3] Certification must be submitted no later than the registration period for the student's final semester at NC State. [3, 5]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Requirements: To declare a minor at North Carolina State University, students should consult with their academic advisor. The general process does not involve a formal application with documents like a resume or statement of purpose, but rather the completion of required coursework. Specific course requirements for the Anthropology minor should be confirmed with the Department of Sociology and Anthropology and an academic advisor.

ProgramName: Minor in Applied Ecology
Requirements: For admission, students should first complete BIO 181 and BIO 360 with letter grades of C-. To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. [1] Application for admission to any University minor program is now available via MyPack Portal. [1] Admission will be based upon the student's academic record, and in most cases no longer requires departmental review. [1]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The minor in Applied Ecology is intended for students interested in applying ecological concepts and principles to solving real-world problems. [2, 4] Students with expertise in applied ecology will be well equipped to address local and global challenges associated with a wide variety of important issues such as water quantity and quality, natural resource management, environmental conservation and restoration, climate change, and maintenance of biodiversity. [2, 4] To receive a minor in Applied Ecology students will be required to complete challenging courses and an in-depth research experience. [2, 4]

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Art and Design
Requirements: The Department of Media Arts, Design and Technology offers courses to all students in the university a minor in Art and Design. Minors are guided through a selection of courses with the consultation from a design adviser. [8, 9]
Description: To meet this need, the department offers an undergraduate minor in Art + Design, available to university students in majors offered outside of the College of Design. The minor in Art + Design consists of 15 total credit hours of study, of which 6 hours must be satisfied at the basic course level. The remaining 9 hours of courses may be selected from the elective course list provided below. A grade of “B” or better will be required for credit in all courses in the minor. [1]
CostPerCredit: The cost per credit hour varies for undergraduate students based on residency. Please refer to the official North Carolina State University tuition and fees schedule for the most current rates.
ScholarshipType: The College of Design offers scholarships to its students, which are primarily merit-based. Students in the Art and Design minor may be eligible for these scholarships.

ProgramName: Minor in Arts Entrepreneurship
Requirements: Students are required to meet with the Arts Entrepreneurship Minor Coordinator to discuss the expectations established for the Arts Entrepreneurship Minor and apply prior to being enrolled in the Minor. [1]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: In addition to examining arts and arts-related industries, the Minor guides students in recognizing opportunities in the arts economies and provides perspectives concerning art's role in society, both as an aesthetic object and a commercial product. [6] Likewise, the Minor helps students to reconsider either their role as artists in communities or their role in providing innovation to the production of art, by introducing the concept of the entrepeneurial artist-citizen. [6] Students are also introduced to the challenges and rewards of being an emerging arts entrepreneur through the Capstone Experience Course. [6] As a program designed for the entire student body, the Arts Entrepreneurship Minor is a rigorous course of study for students interested in exploring entrepreneurial opportunities in the arts and arts-related fields, regardless of their major course of study. [6]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Minor in Arts Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the Minor in Arts Studies, a student must be a current undergraduate at North Carolina State University. Students can apply for admission through the MyPack Portal, and admission is based on the student's academic record. [1] The program requires the completion of 18 credit hours in arts studies with a grade of 'C' or better. [1]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Fees: $9,027.50 per year for in-state residents and $32,997.50 per year for out-of-state residents for the 2025-2026 academic year.
Description: The College of Humanities and Social Sciences offers an academic minor in Arts Studies to all NC State undergraduate majors. This interdisciplinary minor is designed to enrich the student's university experience, to serve as a foundation for learning and understanding in the arts beyond the university years and to provide a line of thinking and skill development that may contribute to the development provided by the student's courses in the major or that may be only loosely related to the major.
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the undergraduate cost per credit hour for in-state residents is $272.29 in tuition and $103.85 in fees for the first credit hour. For out-of-state residents, it is $1,312.50 in tuition and $103.85 in fees for the first credit hour. [8]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available through the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. [19] The Department of Performing Arts and Technology also offers scholarships for students pursuing a music minor. [20]

ProgramName: Minor in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Students who plan to minor in Biological Sciences can do so by using the online CODA system, available through MyPack Portal. [2]
Description: An undergraduate minor in Biological Sciences that is intended to enhance the programs of students whose major fields are outside the biological sciences. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Biomanufacturing
Requirements: To be eligible to apply for the minor, students must have completed at least 12 credit hours at NC State University, completed BIO 183 AND CH 101 (or 103) with a C- or better, and have a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA. [1] To meet preferred requirements, students must have completed at least 12 credit hours at NC State University, completed BIO 183 AND CH 101 (or 103) AND CH 221 (or CH 227) with a C- or better, and have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. [1] A minimum of 15 credit hours is required to earn the minor, and all courses must be completed with a grade of 'C-' or higher. [2, 3]
Description: The undergraduate minor in biomanufacturing was specifically designed to educate and train students in all aspects of biomanufacturing. With a heavy focus on in-depth and hands-on learning opportunities, our students learn to support the large-scale production of biopharmaceutical products while following FDA regulations and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMP). As such, students are well prepared to enter the industry and begin their careers. Students who complete our undergraduate minor gain the following competencies: Overview of Biomanufacturing; Microbiology and Molecular Biology: Expression Systems & Genetic Engineering; Upstream Processing: Cell Growth and Optimization; Downstream Processing: Recovery and Purification; Industry Standards: Equipment, Regulations & CGMP. After completing introductory courses, students choose a specialization area in either upstream or downstream processing to further develop their expertise in highly valued areas in the biomanufacturing industry.

ProgramName: Minor in Biomedical Engineering
Description: The NC State catalog does not provide a detailed description for the Minor in Biomedical Engineering. It outlines the course requirements for the Master's and Doctoral level minors. For a Master's minor, nine credit hours of BME courses at the 500-level or above are required. For a Doctoral minor, fifteen credit hours of BME courses at the 500-level or above are required. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Biotechnology
Requirements: To declare the 'Minor in Biotechnology' at North Carolina State University, students must be current undergraduates and should visit the Student Services 'Add a Minor' page before applying for graduation. The requirements for the minor include preparatory courses such as BIO 183 and CH 223, eight credits of biotechnology lab classes, a three-credit research experience (or an approved alternative), and a one-credit biotechnology ethics course. [8]
Department: The undergraduate Minor in Biotechnology is a university-wide program. [2]
