ProgramName: Minor in Business Administration
Requirements: The minor in Business Administration requires 18 hours of coursework with a 2.0 GPA in minor coursework. [15]
Description: Students who fulfill the requirements for the undergraduate minor in Business Administration will gain an understanding of the language and basic concepts of business, fundamentals of economics, and core concepts of financial accounting. Building on that core foundation, students will pursue additional coursework in several areas of business. The minor in Business Administration requires 18 hours of coursework with a 2.0 GPA in minor coursework.

ProgramName: Minor in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the minor will require 12 completed hours of NC State course work, a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA, and a grade of 'B-' or higher on the first enrollment in CHE 205. [2]
Description: The minor in Chemical Engineering is intended to allow students to develop an understanding of the fundamental concepts and practice of chemical engineering. This minor should prepare undergraduate students in environmental engineering, pulp and paper technology, and chemistry for graduate study in chemical engineering with a minimum amount of prerequisite work following their acceptance into the graduate program. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: The Goodnight Scholars Program for transfer students is valued at $20,000. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Minor in Chinese Studies
Requirements: To declare a minor in Chinese Studies, students must have a GPA of 2.0 or better. The minor requires the completion of 16 credit hours. At least 8 hours of these courses must be taken at NC State. A grade of C- or better is required in all minor courses. The same course cannot be used to satisfy requirements for both the major and the minor.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: Students in any area of study at NC State are eligible to minor in Chinese Studies. The minor in Chinese Studies will provide students with an opportunity to round out their study of Chinese language, culture, and political thought. An investigation of the significance of Modern Asia forms an important complement to studies in Economics, Political Science, History, and Multi-disciplinary Studies. At the completion of the minor the student will: Be able to communicate using the basic skills of modern standard Chinese,; Have some familiarity with Chinese culture, literature and political thought and; Have a general overview of China's political and religious institutions and the role of China in Southeast Asia. [4]
MinGPA: C- or better in all courses in the minor program

ProgramName: Minor in Classical Greek
Requirements: After a thorough search of the North Carolina State University website (catalog.ncsu.edu), a program for a 'Minor in Classical Greek' could not be found. Therefore, no application requirements are available.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Classical Studies
Requirements: Application for admission to any University minor program is available via MyPack Portal and is based on the student's academic record, in most cases not requiring departmental review. Students can declare the minor when they are enrolled in a class that counts towards it. The minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours with a grade of “C-” or better in all courses. A maximum of two courses may be double-counted between major and minor requirements.
Description: The minor in Classical Studies scandals is an excellent foundation for advanced work in other academic disciplines as well as professional programs in law, medicine and management. [4] By presenting a broad selection of courses in the various disciplines of language, literature, philosophy, religious studies and history, the minor provides students with a sound introduction to study of the ancient world. [4, 12] Because of the continuity between ancient and modern cultures, it also gives students an opportunity to develop a keener perception and better understanding of the cultural forces at work in the contemporary world. [4, 12] Depending on their other undergraduate or career goals, students will have the option of pursuing one or more of three concentrations within the Classical Studies minor: Greek, Latin or Classical Culture. [4, 12] The Concentrations in Greek and Latin focus on intensive study of the ancient languages, with significant additional exposure to Classical literature and culture in translation. [4, 12] The Concentration in Classical Culture offers the option of pursuing more general study of Classical literature and culture mostly or exclusively in translation. [4, 12]

ProgramName: Minor in Coaching Education
Requirements: The Coaching Education minor requires the completion of 16 credit hours. [3] Students will complete six credit hours from the three required courses. [3] Students will complete 10 credit hours from eleven elective courses. [3] All minor program courses must be taken for a letter grade. [3] Students must obtain a grade of “C-” or better in each of the required and elective courses. [3] Students must complete HESM 370 Foundations of Sport Coaching and Instruction, HESM 477 Coaching Concepts, and six credits from the sport science electives category before taking HESM 301 Coaching Practicum. [3] A minimum 10 credit hours must be completed at NC State (including the practicum). [3]
Department: Department of Health and Exercise Studies

ProgramName: Minor in Cognitive Science
Requirements: A minimum of 15 hours is required for the minor in Cognitive Science. Students must maintain a grade of 'C-' or better in each course used toward the minor. Cognitive Science minor courses must include at least 3 of the 5 primary disciplines: philosophy (including logic), psychology, computer science, linguistics, and neurobiology. A maximum of TWO (2) courses may double-count between major departmental requirements and courses counting toward the minor. A maximum of TWO (2) courses may double-count between courses counting toward this minor and additional minors. The department will determine whether courses which have been transferred from other institutions qualify for the minor. No more than two courses from other institutions may count toward the minor. No courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit. [11]
Department: Interdisciplinary program involving the departments of Philosophy, Psychology, Linguistics, Biology, and Information Technology

ProgramName: Minor in Communication
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Programming
Requirements: Undergraduates who have completed CODA into a degree program except for Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Engineering can apply for the Minor in Computer Programming via MyPackPortal. Students must complete [E 115 (grade of S) or COS 100 (grade of C minus or higher)], and Calculus I [MA 121, MA 131, or MA 141 -- grade of D minus or higher], and CSC 116 with a grade of C or higher. The overall GPA should be at least 2.25. [1, 7]

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science
Description:
The Department of Computer Science offers a Minor in Computer Programming (CPM) to undergraduate majors in any field except Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Engineering. The minor requires 19 hours of coursework from the Computer Science core. The objectives of this minor are to:

1. Encourage students to combine computing with their own disciplines.
2. Promote quality and process when developing computing solutions.
3. Give graduating seniors with a minor in computer programming an added advantage in the job market. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Conservation
Minor in Creative Writing
Requirements: Students can apply for admission to any university minor program in MyPack Portal. [30] Admission will be based on the student's academic record, and in most cases no longer requires departmental review. [30] The minor requires a minimum of 15 hours, and students must have an overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor and may count no course grade lower than a 'C-'. [29]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in Creative Writing is available from the English Department for NC State students, except for English majors in the Creative Writing concentration. [6]

ProgramName: Minor in Criminology
Requirements: To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. The Criminology minor consists of 16 hours. A 2.0 GPA is required in the minor course work. No courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit. A minimum of 9 hours required course work must be taken at NC State, 3 hours of which must be 400 level. Students completing a major in Sociology (B.A. or B.S.) may not minor in Criminology. [3]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Fees: $4,409.89 per semester for in-state residents, $15,904.89 per semester for out-of-state residents
Description: The criminology minor emphasizes criminological theory and research and is an introduction to the concept of deviance and related issues of criminal behavior. The minor is grounded in sociological theory and methods and allows students flexibility in the choice of specialized criminological study such as, juvenile delinquency, sociology of law, formal institutions of social control, community and crime, and data analysis in criminology. No courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit. [3]
CostPerCredit: $288.39 for in-state residents, $1,262.14 for out-of-state residents

ProgramName: Minor in Crop Science
Requirements: Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better. [1, 3] Students should contact the Crop and Soil Sciences Undergraduate Programs Office to inquire about adding the minor. [1, 3] A minimum of 16 credit hours are required, and a minimum grade of 'C-' is necessary for each course. [1, 3] Students majoring in Agroecology and Sustainable Food Systems (11ASFSBS), Crop and Soil Sciences (11CSSCBS), and Natural Resources - Soil, Water and Land Use (11NATRLBS) are not eligible to enroll in this minor. [1, 3]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The undergraduate minor in Crop Science requires the completion of 16 credit hours and is for students with a general interest in agriculture. [4] A grade of ‘C’ or better is required in all courses for the minor. The minor is available to all baccalaureate students except those in the Crop and Soil Sciences-Crop Production curriculum. The Crop Science minor is not available to students pursuing the B.S. in Agricultural Science.
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarship amounts vary; some are for $1,000, while others cover the full cost of tuition, room, board, and books. [2, 8]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships are available based on academic merit, financial need, and leadership potential. [2, 8]

ProgramName: Minor in Dance
Requirements: Current NC State students can use the self-service Change of Degree Application (CODA) portal to add the dance minor to their degree plan. [2] For the Dance Studies Minor, the requirements include the completion of 15 credit hours with a minimum overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor, and a grade of “C-” or better in each course. [3] For the Dance Performance and Choreography Minor, the requirements include the completion of 17 credit hours with a minimum overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor, and a grade of “C-” or better in each course. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Design Studies
Minor in Economics
Requirements: To declare a minor in economics, students must have a GPA of 2.0 or better. The minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours. Required courses include EC 201 and EC 202, or ARE 201. Students must also complete nine additional credit hours in economics at the 300 or 400 level, with at least one course at the 400 level. A grade of 'C-' or better is required in all minor courses.
Description: TThe minor in Economics is designed to help students develop a basic understanding of the principles and applications of economics. By pursuing this minor the student will: develop an understanding of microeconomic and macroeconomic theory and the role of markets: understand the effects of government regulation and policy on economic behavior; learn to apply economics to contemporary social and market issues; and develop analytical skills.

ProgramName: Minor in Education
Minor in English
Requirements: To be admitted to the English minor, students must apply through MyPack Portal, and admission is based on their academic record. The program requires the completion of 15 hours of coursework at or above the 200 level. A maximum of two courses (6 credit hours) can be from transfer credits. Students must maintain an overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor and cannot have a grade lower than 'C-'. A maximum of two courses can be double-counted between major requirements and the minor.
Description: The English Department offers a minor in English to majors in any field except English. The minor program will allow students to pursue general interests in writing, literature, and language. [3, 8]

ProgramName: Minor in Entomology
Requirements: The undergraduate minor in Entomology requires 15 semester hours. A grade of 'C-' or better is required for all courses to fulfill the minor requirements. Students must take either ENT 425 General Entomology or ENT 402 Forest Entomology, plus 12 hours from an elective course list, of which at least 6 hours must be ENT courses. [4] Application for admission is available through MyPack Portal and is based on the student's academic record. [4]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: An undergraduate minor in Entomology is offered for students interested in insects and their diversity, ecology, behavior, management, and their role in the functioning of natural and agricultural ecosystems. Insects are the single largest group of animal species, impacting every aspect of human life and are a crucial part of our environment. This minor provides an opportunity for students to become familiar with this fascinating group of organisms. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Science
Requirements: Any student with an interest in the Environmental Science minor should see the contact person to discuss their interest, course requirements, and complete the Declaration of Minor form. Students must have a minimum overall grade point average of 2.0 to be admitted to the minor. [5, 7] The minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours from approved courses. [5]
Description: The Environmental Sciences minor allows students to connect the topics from their major to the compelling, contemporary issues that connect humans to the environment. The minor includes courses in all academic units to provide links between disciplines and to provide a foundation for analysis of environmental issues. [8, 9]

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Toxicology
Requirements: NCSU undergraduate students may be admitted to the minor after successfully completing 60 credit hours. Students must download and complete the Minor Application Form and return it to the Undergraduate Program Coordinator. [4] The minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours, with nine hours from required courses and six hours from electives. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Extension Education
Requirements: The minor in Extension Education is open to all interested baccalaureate students. [3] The minor requires a minimum of 15 credit hours, and the minimum grade for all courses counting toward the minor is a 'C'. [3] Current students can use the Change of Degree Application (CODA) to add, change or drop minors. [3]
Department: Department of Agricultural and Human Sciences
Fees: A minimum grade of “C” is required for all courses counting toward the minor. [1]
Description: The minor inExtensionEducation is open to all interested baccalaureate students. The minor is especially appropriate for students interested in careers with the CooperativeExtensionSystem or other nonformal educational/community outreach organizations. The minor is especially appealing for those students in majors that touchExtension's core programs of agriculture and food, health and nutrition, and 4-H youth development, including: Agricultural Education; Agricultural Science; Agricultural and Resource Economics; Animal Science; Applied Ecology; Biological and Agricultural Engineering; Community Development; Communication; Crop and Soil Sciences; Family and Community Sciences; Food, Bioprocessing and Nutrition Sciences; Forest Biomaterials; Forestry and Environmental Resources; Entomology and Plant Pathology; Horticultural Science; Health and Exercise Studies; Landscape Architecture; Parks, Recreation, and Tourism; Poultry Science; Public Administration; Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Education; Textile and Apparel. Students completing a minor inExtensionEducation will become familiar with the organization, structure, and mission of CooperativeExtension; planning and delivery of nonformal educational programs; management and leadership of volunteers; communication media and technology; and leadership theory, principles, and skills. Courses used to satisfy the minor may not be taken for credit only. Course substitutions may be made with minor advisor and minor administrator approval.

ProgramName: Minor in Film Studies
Requirements: Students can apply for admission to the minor program in MyPack Portal. Admission is based on the student's academic record and generally does not require departmental review. [14] The program requires the completion of 15 credit hours at the 200 level or above, with no more than 6 transfer hours. The program aims to help students order and integrate the diverse aspects of their educational programs, explore the moral dimensions of scientific inquiry and technological design and deployment, appreciate the practical implications of scientific theories, and increase their breadth of their interests in science and technology. [16, 23] The program is designed to help students understand the connections among science, technology, economics, domestic policy, international relations, the environment, health and medicine, and other crucial areas. [23] Students in the minor will examine how science and technology emerge, how they engage with society, how they change through social processes and how society changes under their influence. [23]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Social Work
Requirements: A total of 16 hours (5 courses) is required for the minor. Four required courses (13 credit hours) and one SW Elective (3 credit hours). A grade of 'C' or better must be achieved in each class counting toward the minor and an overall GPA of 2.5 must be maintained in the minor courses. All courses in the minor must be taken for a letter grade. [6] Application for admission to the minor program is available via MyPack Portal and is based upon the student's academic record. [6]
Description: A minor is not available in this program.The Minor in Social Work is designed to familiarize students with the social service system, major social welfare programs, and elements of the profession of social work. This is an excellent minor for students interested in combining a primary academic area (major), such as sociology, political science, or psychology with social welfare and professional social work content. It is also an excellent field of study for students majoring in any area who many need or desire knowledge of social welfare and social services.No courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit.

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Requirements: The sociology minor consists of 16 hours of coursework. To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. Application for admission is available via MyPack Portal. Any student seeking a minor must consult with a minor advisor to create a plan of work. A 2.0 GPA is required for all minor coursework, and no courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit. At least 9 hours of the required coursework must be completed at NC State, with 3 of those hours at the 400 level. Students completing a major in Criminology may not minor in Sociology. [5]
Description: The sociology minor emphasizes sociological theory and research with substantive applications. The minor builds on theory and methodology and allows students flexibility in the choice of sub-disciplines such as criminology, stratification, demography, social psychology, race and ethnic relations, or the family. No courses for the minor may be taken for S/U credit.

ProgramName: Minor in Soil Science
Requirements: Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better. Students should contact the Crop and Soil Sciences Undergraduate Programs Office to inquire about adding the minor no later than the registration period for the student's final semester at NC State.
Description: The minor in Soil Science is offered to all undergraduate students at NC State University, with the exception of those enrolled in a major within the Department of Crop & Soil Science. The minor strengthens the understanding of basic physical, chemical, and microbiological soil properties that would be relevant to a student's particular land management interest. The Soil Science minor is a perfect complement for students majoring in Biological and Agricultural Engineering, Environmental Science, Forestry, Geology, Horticulture, or Landscape Architecture.

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Requirements: To declare a minor in Spanish at North Carolina State University, students must have a declared major. The minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours of coursework. This includes FLS 331 and FLS 332. The remaining 9 credits must be at the 300 or 400 level. Up to 6 of these 15 credits may be transfer credits, but they must be from a 4-year institution and approved by the Department of Foreign Languages and Literatures.
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description:
The minor in Spanish requires the completion of 15 credit hours from the list of all courses at the 300 and 400 levels taught in Spanish, with the following requirements:

1. At least two of the five courses must be at the 400-level.
2. All courses must be taught in Spanish.
3. The minor may not include courses taught in English, such as FL 495.
4. FLS 332, while it may be a prerequisite for some 400-level courses, may not be included in the minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Statistics
Requirements: Admission requirements for the minor: At least 12 NCSU hours passed. Cumulative GPA of at least 2.0. Completion of either ST 312 or 372 with a grade of B or higher. GPA of 3.0 or higher for all ST courses. [8]
Description: The minor program of study teaches students to use statistical methods and software to solve real-world data analysis problems. The statistics and analytics tools that form the heart of this program are routinely applied to subjects including business and finance, biomedical science, sports analytics, sociology, education, and engineering. A flexible academic plan offers almost all students at NC State access to this valuable minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Sustainable Energy
Minor in Sustainable Materials
Requirements: To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. [1] Application for admission to any University minor program is now available via MyPack Portal. [1] Admission will be based upon the student's academic record, and in most cases no longer requires departmental review. [1]
Description: The Department of Forest Biomaterials (FB) offers a minor in Sustainable Materials and Technology (SMT) to all undergraduates enrolled in the University as degree candidates except those in FB. The minor will provide students with a basic understanding of sustainability as applied to materials (e.g., wood, agricultural products, etc.) and the manufacturing processes that are used to convert them into a multitude of different products. [1]
CostPerCredit: Undergraduates will be charged $62.50 per credit hour ($750.00 for full-time 12+ hours).

ProgramName: Minor in Textile Technology
Requirements: To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. [2] Undergraduate students enrolled in all programs at NC State University are eligible to take this minor. [2] Application for admission to any university minor program is now available via MyPack Portal. [2] A grade of 'C-' or better is required in all courses to be used towards this minor. [2]
Description: The Department of Textile Engineering Chemistry and Science offers students the opportunity to minor in Textile Technology. Undergraduate students enrolled in all programs at NC State University are eligible to take this minor. The minor allows students to explore the principles of textile technology and develop technical textile products. Students also have the opportunity to use textile technology facilities as part of the minor. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Minor in Theatre
Requirements: To declare a minor in Theatre, students must fill out an electronic 'Intent to Pursue a Minor Form'. This form needs to be approved by both the Theatre Minor Advisor and the academic advisor in the student's home college. The process may be completed electronically. [1]
Department: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Minor in Theatre offers students a comprehensive overview of the study of theatre, including both academic (history and criticism) and production (acting, design and technology) courses. The purpose is to expose undergraduate students to the field by reinforcing the integrated nature of theatre as a scholarly and aesthetic pursuit. Students are required to take a core of 10 required hours in courses that prepare them academically to understand the theoretic and historical basis of the art. They then take a minimum of six hours of electives in two general areas (History/Criticism and Production/Performance) with at least one course from each area. This ensures that every theatre minor has not only some choice of specialization, but also a breadth of knowledge required of all theatre professionals.

ProgramName: Minor in Turfgrass Science
Requirements: The minor in Turf Grass Science is open to all undergraduate students at NC State University, with the exception of those enrolled in the Turfgrass Science major. Admission to the minor requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or better. [2]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: TThe mirror is open to all undergraduate students at NC State University, with the exception of those enrolled in the Turfgrass Science major. It is designed for students majoring in Plant and Soil Sciences, Biological Sciences, Horticultural Science, Parks & Recreation and related disciplines but will be of interest to a wide variety of students desiring expertise in establishing and maintaining turfgrass areas. Students will gain an understanding of the techniques required to successfully establish and manage turfgrasses commonly grown throughout the United States. This knowledge will improve the student's ability to provide high quality turfgrass cover for a variety of situations including home lawns, commercial grounds, parks and other areas.

ProgramName: Minor in US Diversity
Minor in Water Resources
Requirements: The interdisciplinary, interdepartmental graduate minor in water resources is designed for students majoring in the many disciplines of natural resources, science, engineering, technology, and social sciences that are relevant to water resources. [4] The graduate minor in water resources (WR) requires successful completion (“B-” or better in each individual WR course, GPA of 3.0 or better across all WR courses counted toward the minor) of at least 9 credits of WR courses. [4] At least 3 of the 9 credits (for M.S. students) or 6 of the 9 credits (for Ph.D. students) must be from outside the student's major department. [4]
Concentration: ['Hydrological and Meteorological Aspects of Water Resources', 'Water Quality Aspects of Water Resources', 'Biological and Ecological Aspects of Water Resources', 'Legal, Institutional, and Economic Aspects of Water Resources']
Description: The interdisciplinary, interdepartmental graduate minor in water resources is designed for students majoring in the many disciplines of natural resources, science, engineering, technology, and social sciences that are relevant to water resources. The minor exposes students to water resources courses and faculty members within and outside their major fields of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Wildlife Science
Requirements: Students must have a GPA of 2.0 or above to be admitted into the minor. The wildlife minor is not available to Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology majors. Interested and eligible students can Add a Minor in MyPack Portal. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Women's and Gender Studies
Description: The Women's and Gender Studies Minor offers all students in the university the possibility of rigorous interdisciplinary study of women's and gender issues. [4] Course offerings across the campus give students the opportunity to understand the complex relationships between gender, class, ethnic, and race structures; to understand feminist theory and methodological perspectives and their substantial contributions to social and public policy analysis; to develop the ability to reach out to community and non-profit organizations concerned with social equality; and to develop international understandings and perspectives. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in World and Comparative Literature
Requirements: NC State is test-optional for first-year applicants with a weighted high school GPA of 2.8 or higher. First-year applicants with a weighted GPA between 2.5 and 2.79 are required to submit a standardized test score. [4] The SAT Essay or ACT Writing sections are not required. [4] Application requirements for graduate programs are largely determined by the specific program of interest, and applicants should consult the individual program for a list of required materials.

ProgramName: Minor in Zoology
Requirements: To be admitted to the program, a student must have a GPA of at least 2.0. Application for admission to any University minor program is now available via MyPack Portal. Admission will be based upon the student's academic record, and in most cases no longer requires departmental review. [3]
Department: Department of Biological Sciences in the College of Sciences. [5]
Description: The Department of Biological Sciences in the College of Sciences offers an undergraduate minor in Zoology intended to enhance the programs of students who are interested in obtaining a solid foundation in zoological concepts, including diversity in the animal kingdom, animal behavior, and the comparative physiology of animals. [3] It is open to all baccalaureate students except those majoring in Zoology (17ZOOBS) or Biological Sciences with a concentration in Ecology, Evolution, and Conservation Biology (17BIOSCEEC). [3]
